jobs.title: Director of Operations (with COO development track)
jobs.description:
Curtis Legal Group is seeking a strategic, driven, and enthusiastic, Director of

Operations to join our personal injury practice and serve as an operational leader

supporting the firm’s C\-Suite, attorneys, and legal teams. This role is designed for

an operations leader who thrives in translating firm strategy into scalable systems,

clear accountability, and consistent execution across legal teams.

Curtis Legal Group values collaboration, integrity, clarity, and high standards. The

Director of Operations plays a critical role in strengthening how legal work is

supported, supervised, and delivered without practicing law or directing legal

judgment.

**Position Overview**

The Director of Operations is a position tracking to the position of Chief Operations

Officer (COO). This person is responsible for assisting stakeholders with firm\-wide

oversight of legal support operations, case workflow execution, performance

management, and cross\-functional alignment between attorneys, operations,

finance, intake, and administration. This role focuses on optimizing legal delivery

systems, improving consistency across offices and teams, and supporting attorney

effectiveness and capacity.

**Reporting Relationship**

Reports directly to the C\-Suite team of the Firm.

**Authority \& Scope**

* Assists operations across all practice locations
* Establishes firm\-wide legal operational standards, workflows, and KPIs
* Deploys artificial intelligence solutions
* Partners with legal leadership on execution while respecting attorney autonomy and ethical boundaries
* Reviews and provides analysis of firm operations, including budgets in order to develop efficiencies and to scale profitability
* Creates innovative solutions for firm operations and reviews data analytics, including use of AI support
* Serves as the C\-Suite representative of the management team and oversees office work culture in the Sacramento office
* Assists management team with firm marketing strategies and advertising
* mediums

**Core Responsibilities**

**Operations Leadership**

* Assists in oversight of the execution and consistency of legal workflows from intake handoff through case resolution
* Monitors KPIs including but not limited to firm’s AI usage, client service, attorney revenue, case progression, attorney and legal team caseload capacity, case resolution time and obstacles
* Collaborates with Managing Attorneys to align operational systems with legal strategy and client outcomes
* Develops and maintains standard operating procedures (SOPs) supporting legal teams
* Assists HR to recruit and develop existing and future team members
* People Leadership \& Accountability
* Assists with development of legal operation supervisors, managers, case managers, and support leaders
* Demonstrates and advocates firm values in the role as a leader of team members
* Supports attorney performance through clarity of roles, expectations, and tools—not legal direction
* Drives, manages, and demonstrates a growth mindset in firm performance, training, mentorship, and professional development
* Cross\-Functional \& Strategic Support
* Acts as the primary operational liaison between legal teams and firm leadership
* Partners on firm planning, staffing models, budgeting inputs, and growth initiatives
* Creates and develops operational efficiencies and strategy for firm profitability

**Qualifications**

* Master's degree in business administration (MBA) /management or demonstrated operational leadership experience
* Exhibits and/or demonstrates skills required for success in leading
* operational teams
* Experience in professional services or legal services
* Experience with artificial intelligence (AI) programs and systems
* Understanding of business budgets and accounting systems
* Proficient in Microsoft suite programs
* Experience with leading teams

**Location \& Compensation**

**Location:** Sacramento, CA

Schedule: Possibly hybrid remote depending on experience leading teams remotely.

**Travel requirements:** Travel to the Modesto periodically.

**Compensation:** $90,000 \- $120,000 annually (commensurate with experience)

**How to Apply:** Submit Indeed application including the following:

* Your resume
* A cover letter (no more than one page) explaining why you would be a strong fit for this role
* Email subject line must read: “Director of Operations”
* Applications that do not follow these instructions will not be considered.

Pay: $90,000\.00 \- $120,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* How would you define effective leadership?
* Do you meet the minimum requirements of the position?
* How many years of leadership experience do you have?
* How many years of legal office experience do you have?
* How would you rate your AI competency from 1\-10 ( 10 being fully mastered and 1 being very limited)?

Education:

* Master's (Preferred)

Experience:

* Law office: 3 years (Preferred)

Location:

* Sacramento, CA 95825 (Preferred)

Willingness to travel:

* 25% (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: VP of Development
jobs.description:
**Position:** VP of Development

**Organization:** Junior Achievement of Northern California Location: Bay Area, CA (Hybrid / Highly Community\-Facing) **Reports To:** CEO/President **Base Salary Range:** $140,000 \- $160,000 (Commensurate with executive experience and proven revenue history)

**About JA NorCal**

At Junior Achievement of Northern California, our purpose is to inspire and prepare young people to succeed in a global economy. We are actively building the future of Northern California’s workforce through experiential learning, AI skilling, and financial literacy.

Our culture is deeply collaborative, ambitious, and action\-oriented. We move thoughtfully and efficiently, balancing big\-picture vision with practical execution. We believe our greatest impact happens through strong community relationships and a shared commitment to serving students and partners.

**Position Overview**

Junior Achievement of Northern California is at a critical inflection point of expansion. As we build our 13,000 sq. ft. JA Launchpad in Fremont, navigate the AB2927 state mandate, and deepen our impact, we are seeking a visionary and results\-oriented fundraising leader who thrives in a dynamic environment and can help fuel our growth.

The VP of Development is an executive role designed to scale our annual revenue from $3M to $5M\+ in the next three years. Serving as the CEO's strategic partner and a key external representative of JA NorCal, the VP of Development will bring strategic vision, operational discipline, and a data\-informed approach to fundraising. This leader will guide capital campaign efforts, strengthen donor engagement and stewardship, oversee signature fundraising events, and secure transformational support from institutional, corporate, government, and individual funders.

If you are someone who understands the intersection of corporate ROI and philanthropic impact—and you thrive on being out in the community building partnerships and closing deals—this is your opportunity to build the financial engine for the future of our workforce.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1\. Front\-Line Revenue Generation \& Executive Closing**

* Serve as the lead external fundraiser for JA NorCal, actively identifying, cultivating, and closing five\- and six\-figure gifts to achieve a $5M\+ annual revenue target within the next three years.
* Take direct ownership of the JA Launchpad Capital Campaign, successfully securing the remaining funding and actively driving the financial timeline for our grand opening.
* Government Funding Strategy: Help create a strategy to identify, navigate, and secure lucrative local, state, and federal government grants that align with our workforce development mission and programmatic expansion.
* Act as a compelling, forward\-facing spokesperson for the organization at major events, corporate pitches, and community forums.

**2\. Event Strategy \& Sponsorship Management**

* Executive Event Oversight: Direct the strategic vision and execution of JA NorCal’s major fundraising and cultivation events (including the annual Golf for Good tournament), transforming them into high\-ROI, brand\-elevating experiences.
* Corporate Sponsorships: Lead the strategic packaging, pitching, and fulfillment of high\-level event and program sponsorships, ensuring corporate partners receive exceptional visibility, engagement, and ROI.
* Ensure all events serve as strategic touchpoints integrated into the broader capital campaign to accelerate pipeline velocity.

**3\. Executive Department Leadership \& Mentorship**

* Oversee, mentor, and manage the Development team, strengthening an already collaborative and results\-oriented approach to fundraising and donor engagement.
* Partner with program and leadership teams to strengthen impact measurement, storytelling, and donor stewardship efforts, ensuring funders receive compelling evidence of outcomes alongside meaningful engagement and follow\-up. Act as the strategic buffer and "closer" for the Development staff, stepping into major pitch meetings to articulate the business case for investment.

**4\. Financial Acumen \& Pipeline Rigor**

* Oversee fundraising forecasting and pipeline management, providing leadership and the Board with accurate, timely insights into revenue projections, funding opportunities, and fundraising performance.
* Partner with program and leadership teams to develop compelling impact narratives that demonstrate the value and outcomes of JA NorCal's programs to key funders and partners.
* Partner with Finance and Operations to ensure fundraising strategies are aligned with organizational priorities, resource needs, and long\-term sustainability.

**5\. Executive Strategy \& Board Partnership**

* Serve on the JA NorCal Executive Leadership Team, partnering closely with the CEO to set the long\-term strategic and financial vision for the organization.
* Engage and activate the Board of Directors in the fundraising process, giving them the tools, confidence, and specific targets they need to leverage their networks effectively.

**Qualifications**

* 5\+ years of senior leadership experience in corporate social responsibility (CSR), corporate finance, wealth management, or high\-level nonprofit development.
* A proven, quantifiable track record of closing major gifts and/or corporate sponsorships ($250k\+) and scaling organizational/departmental revenue.
* Event Leadership: Experience providing executive oversight for large\-scale, high\-revenue fundraising events and securing major corporate sponsorships.
* Demonstrated ability to use data, financial insights, and program outcomes to develop compelling funding strategies and donor partnerships.
* A relationship\-oriented leader who enjoys building partnerships, engaging with donors and community stakeholders, and serving as a visible ambassador for JA NorCal.
* An empathetic and accountable leader with experience managing and developing high\-performing teams.

**C

jobs.title: Executive Director Non Profit Organization
jobs.description:
**About Art Division**
**Art Division** is a nonprofit 501(c)(3\) organization dedicated to training and supporting under\-served youth (ages 18–27\) who are committed to studying the visual arts. We believe that focused instruction, individualized tutoring, and personal support empower students to pursue higher education, achieve self\-sufficiency, and establish careers in the arts and related fields.
Art Division is at a pivotal point in its growth—poised to deepen its programming, expand its fundraising capacity, and strengthen its internal operations. This is an exciting opportunity for a leader who is energized by helping a mission\-driven organization evolve and thrive. We are also deeply committed to community engagement and building a thriving arts ecosystem in the Rampart District of Los Angeles.
**Position Summary**
We are seeking a passionate, culturally aware, and locally based **Director** with a fine arts background and experience in nonprofit or community arts. This is a part\-time role (32 hours a week Tuesday through Friday) , ideal for someone who is fluent in Spanish, collaborative, and aligned with Art Division’s mission to uplift underserved youth through the arts. The Director will report to the Board of Directors and serve as the public\-facing leader of Art Division, working closely with staff, artists, and partners to drive the mission forward. For at least six months they will work alongside Dan McCleary, the current director.
**Key Qualifications**  

* Proven experience cultivating individual donors (fundraising)
* 5–7\+ years of nonprofit or community arts experience
* Bilingual (Spanish/English)
* Background in fine arts (visual/media)
* Reside in Los Angeles and able to work on\-site
* Available for occasional evenings and weekends
* Culturally competent and able to build trust with underserved youth

**Who You Are**
* A creative and empathetic leader with a love for the arts and social equity
* A connector who builds relationships across cultures, generations, and sectors
* Someone who finds joy in mentoring and supporting young artists
* Committed to racial equity and authentic community engagement
* Comfortable wearing many hats in a small, nimble organization

**Key Responsibilities**
**Fundraising \& Resource Development**  

* Collaborate with the Board to develop and execute a fundraising strategy that includes major donors, grants, and foundation partnerships
* Help develop the annual budget and align funding goals with programming needs
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, family foundations, and institutional funders
* Identify and pursue new revenue opportunities through grants, events, and partnerships


  

**Mission \& Strategic Leadership**  

* Collaborate with the Board and staff to ensure programs and initiatives reflect Art Division’s mission and pedagogy
* Advise long\-term strategic planning for organizational sustainability and growth  

Uphold and advance Art Division’s values and cultural integrity within a changing community landscape

**Program Oversight \& Artistic Direction**  

* Ensure program offerings reflect core pedagogy and serve the needs of students (ages 18–27\)
* Support the design of core classes, events, and special projects
* Collaborate with Visual and Media Arts leads to recruit instructors, guest artists, and facilitate lectures, workshops, and field trips
* Provide creative input on exhibition planning in our gasllery

**Board Relations \& Governance**  

* Maintain regular communication with the Board and contribute to effective governance
* Provide leadership and recommendations around organizational challenges and opportunities
* Work with the Board to align operational and artistic direction

**Brand, Design \& Communications**  

* Collaborate with the in\-house designer to maintain brand identity and aesthetic consistency
* Work with the Exhibit Manager on gallery installations and public presentations
* Represent the organization at public events and maintain visibility in the local arts community
* Serve as an articulate and passionate spokesperson for Art Division

**Community Engagement \& Partnerships**  

* Maintain relationships with local partners, city agencies, and community leaders
* Stay active and visible in the Rampart District and broader Los Angeles arts ecosystem
* Create opportunities for Art Division to engage with the community through public programming and outreach

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**InnerRhythms, Inc.**

Contract Term: 12 months, including a 30\-day trial period Annual Contract Amount: $45,000–$52,000

Reports to: Board of Directors

Estimated Time Commitment: Approximately 20/30 hours per week on average.

Hours will vary throughout the year, with a greater time commitment during showcase periods and fewer hours during the summer and other slower months Position Summary The Executive Director provides organizational leadership and oversees the day\-to\-day operations of InnerRhythms. Working closely with the Board of Directors, artistic leadership, instructors, and staff, the ED is responsible for organizational management, fundraising, financial oversight, studio operations, community engagement, and supporting successful programming and performances.

**Key Responsibilities Leadership \& Operations** 

* Manage day\-to\-day operations of the organization and studio.
* Hire, manage, and support staff and instructors.
* Oversee class scheduling, enrollment, tuition, scholarships, communications, and general studio administration.
* Maintain a regular studio presence and serve as a primary contact for students, families, and staff.
* Work with the Board on organizational planning, policies, and long\-term sustainability. Financial Management \& Fundraising
* Oversee budgeting, bookkeeping, payroll, financial reporting, and general financial operations.
* Lead fundraising efforts in collaboration with the Board.
* Develop relationships with donors, funders, sponsors, and community partners.
* Support grant writing, reporting, donor communications, and fundraising events. Programs \& Performances
* Collaborate with artistic leadership and instructors on class programming, curriculum, and student placement.
* Coordinate the operational and logistical aspects of performances, showcases, workshops, and special events.
* Secure venues and coordinate vendors, front\-of\-house activities, and other production needs.
* Support artistic leadership in successfully implementing the creative vision for performances and programs. Marketing \& Community Engagement
* Oversee organizational marketing, communications, and promotional activities.
* Build partnerships with local organizations, schools, businesses, and community groups.
* Represent InnerRhythms at community events and develop opportunities to increase awareness and participation.

**Qualifications** 

* At least five years of nonprofit leadership, management, fundraising, or comparable professional experience.
* Strong organizational, communication, financial management, and leadership skills.
* Demonstrated fundraising experience.
* Experience managing staff, contractors, budgets, and multiple priorities.
* Ability to work collaboratively with a nonprofit Board, staff, instructors, families, and community partners.
* Commitment to InnerRhythms' mission and inclusive approach to dance and arts education.

**Contract \& Compensation** 

This is a 12\-month independent contractor position with an annual contract amount of $45,000–$52,000 , depending on experience. The contract will begin with a 30\-day trial period to ensure the position and working relationship are a good fit for both InnerRhythms and the contractor. The position requires flexibility for studio activities, performances, events, and occasional evening and weekend responsibilities.

To Apply Please submit a resume and cover letter to Kristy Oriol, Interim Executive Director, at info@innerrhythms.org .

Pay: $45,000\.00 \- $52,000\.00 per year

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Part time Executive Director with potential for Full Time

Overview

We are seeking an experienced and dynamic part time Executive Director to lead our

organization towards strategic growth and operational excellence. The ideal candidate will

possess strong management skills, a visionary mindset, and the ability to drive initiatives that

align with our mission.

Organization Description

National Alliance On Mental Illness ( NAMI) of San Luis Obispo County, CA is a 501 c3

nonprofit, grassroots organization dedicated to improving the lives of people with severe and

persistent mental health issues and their loved ones through effective and innovative support,

education, and advocacy. We are family members, loved ones, and those with lived experiences

of many ages, cultures, and stages. Though independent, NAMI SLO County is an affiliate of

NAMI National and NAMI California.

Job Responsibilities

Skills and Dispositions Desired:

 Nonprofit leadership experience

 Familiarity with mental illness as a professional, caregiver, or individual living with a

mental illness

 Follow strategic direction from the Board and set organizational goals in alignment with

mission and vision

 Cultivate relationships, communicate and collaborate effectively with stakeholders,

including, clients, board members, and community leaders

 Ability to collaborate with Board of Directors, staff and community partners

 Experience working with a Board of Directors and following directions of the Board

 Experience with strategic planning

 Drive business development efforts to expand organizational impact and revenue streams

 Fiscal management skills, including budget preparation, decision\-making, and reporting

 Manage budgets, resources, and organizational performance metrics to achieve financial

sustainability

 Experience in developing new revenue streams, fundraising, events, and donor relations

 Strong organizational skills and problem\-solving skills

 Grant writing and program management experience

 Represent the organization at public events, conferences to enhance visibility and

reputation

 Robust work ethic with a sense of passion and urgency regarding bettering systems and

resources for those affected by mental illness, a willingness to learn in areas in which

prior knowledge may not exist

 Strong sense of integrity in leadership \- conviction to lead with compassion, honesty, and

effectiveness.

 Proficiency in working with Microsoft and Google platforms and tools, websites,

Mailchimp and social media.

 Ensure adherence to legal standards and uphold organizational integrity.

 Proven experience in management with a strong background in strategic planning and

operations management. \- both in the legislative nature and personal

 Excellent negotiation skills with the ability to build consensus among diverse

stakeholders.

 Strong business development acumen with a track record of expanding organizational

reach.

 Proficiency in project management and process improvement methodologies.

 Exceptional communication skills with the ability to inspire teams and engage external

partners.

 Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred.

 Ability to think critically, adapt to changing environments, and lead organizational

change effectively.

Qualifications

The Executive Director is a comprehensive leader for the organization and within the

community, responsible for overseeing the programs, administration, and strategic planning for

the good of the organization and all whom it serves. other key attributes of a qualified candidate

include the following:

 Fundraising

 Marketing, Community Outreach, \&Public Relations

 Fiscal Management

 Mental Health Advocacy Work \- both in the legislative nature and personal. Working

closely with families and those affected by mental illness as they navigate resources.

General Responsibilities:

 Responsible for leading NAMI SLO County in a manner consistent with the mission and

vision defined by the Board of Directors

 Responsible for communicating effectively with the Board, providing all necessary

information to the Board to function effectively and efficiently, and to make informed

decisions

 Incorporate principals of Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in all outreach and

engagement work

 Responsible for fundraising and developing other revenue streams necessary to support

the mission of NAMI SLO County

 Responsible for collaborating with treasurer and bookkeeper to oversee fiscal

management of NAMI SLO County

 Responsible for grant writing, grant management and communications

 Responsible for implementing programs that support the organization's mission in

conjunction with the vision and goals of the Board of Directors (keeping in mind the

resource and advocacy needs of those in the community affected by mental illness)

 Responsible for developing and implementing a strategic plan and assessing the plan's

performance (may refer to the current strategic plan with the Board to update as

necessary

 Responsible for enhancing NAMI SLO County's reputation and rapport with the

community including mental health providers through the organization's coordinated,

organizations, and other nonprofits

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
Job Overview

**Mission Focus:** The Development Director plays a critical role in ensuring the long\-term financial sustainability of the organization and expanding resources that improve health outcomes for the communities we serve.

**Position Summary**  
The Development Director is responsible for planning, implementing, and overseeing all fundraising, donor engagement, and development activities to advance the organization’s mission of providing accessible, high\-quality healthcare services to the community. The Development Director will cultivate relationships with donors, foundations, corporations, and community partners to secure financial resources that support organizational sustainability and growth. Evening and weekend hours may be required to meet donors and engage in community events.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Fundraising and Resource Development**

● Develop and execute an annual fundraising plan aligned with organizational priorities and financial goals.

● Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individual, corporate, and foundation donors.

● Lead major gift initiatives and planned giving opportunities.

● Research and pursue grant opportunities and oversee grant writing and reporting.

● Plan and implement annual giving campaigns and special fundraising events.

● Establish fundraising goals and track progress toward achieving revenue targets.

● Coordinate and oversee Grant Contractor to ensure any grant and corporate request are in alignment with the fundraising strategy.

**Donor and Community Relations**

● Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, community leaders, businesses, and philanthropic organizations.

● Develop donor recognition and stewardship programs to strengthen long\-term engagement.

● Serve as an ambassador for the organization within the community.

● Coordinate community outreach initiatives that increase awareness and support of the organization's mission.

**Strategic Leadership**

● Collaborate with the CEO and leadership team to identify funding priorities and strategic opportunities.

● Provide regular reports on fundraising activities, donor engagement, and development metrics.

● Develop and monitor the development budget.

● Ensure fundraising activities comply with all applicable regulations and ethical standards.

**Marketing and Communications**

● Partner with communications staff and or contractor to develop compelling fundraising materials, impact reports, and donor communications.

● Oversee development\-related marketing strategies, including digital campaigns and social media initiatives.

● Communicate the impact of donor support through storytelling and data\-driven reporting.

● Maintain media relationships and support press/PR outreach.

● Ensure the website is optimized for online donations

● Use a metrics\-driven approach to evaluate marketing effectiveness

● Oversee creation of marketing and fundraising materials, including annual impact report and newsletters

**Board Engagement**

● Partner with the Board of Directors to strengthen philanthropic leadership and fundraising participation.

● Support board members in donor cultivation and stewardship activities.

● Assist in developing and implementing board fundraising expectations and initiatives.

**Qualifications**

● Bachelor's degree in Business, Communications, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, or a related field; master's degree preferred.

● Minimum of five years of progressively responsible fundraising and development experience, preferably in healthcare and/or nonprofit organizations.

● Demonstrated success in securing major gifts, grants, and corporate sponsorships.

● Strong relationship\-building, communication, and presentation skills.

● Experience managing fundraising events and donor databases.

● Experience in a small shop organization.

● Knowledge of healthcare funding trends and philanthropic practices.

● Proficiency in Microsoft Office and donor management software.

● Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) or comparable certification preferred, supplemented by an active professional affiliation (e.g. AFP)

**Preferred Attributes**

● Passion for improving access to healthcare and serving diverse communities.

● Strategic thinker with strong organizational and project management skills.

● Collaborative leadership style and ability to work effectively with staff, volunteers, and community stakeholders.

● High degree of integrity, professionalism, and discretion.

**Benefits**

Competitive benefit package.

Join us as our **Development Director**, where your leadership will shape our growth trajectory! We’re committed to empowering our team members through innovative strategies, collaborative culture, and opportunities for professional excellence—all while making a significant impact in the industry!

Pay: $115,000\.00 \- $130,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 403(b)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

The Wealth Client Specialist is a sophisticated wealth expert that focuses on holistically addressing the wealth needs of High Net Worth and Ultra High Net Worth individuals and institutions. This individual has extensive experience in wealth management and effectively introduces appropriate JPMorgan Chase wealth services to best meet the objectives of each client. The Client Specialist provides high level advice and counsel, offers attractive wealth management solutions, and delivers a high level of service.


As a **Wealth Client Specialist within J.P. Morgan Wealth Management**, you will focus on addressing the wealth needs of High Net Worth and Ultra High Net Worth team members and institutions. You will market and sell JPMorgan Chase wealth management services, source new business, and collaborate with a team of professionals to provide high level advice and counsel. You will also keep abreast of trends and strategies in wealth management and engage with other advisors on client engagement efforts. This role requires an autonomous, sophisticated wealth expert who will focus on creating new and deepening existing wealth relationships with high net worth and ultra\-high net worth clients across JP Morgan Wealth Management. You will address clients' wealth considerations, collaborate with colleagues to provide high level advice and counsel, market and sell wealth management services, and ensure we have a holistic view of clients' wealth and planning needs.


Your new business generation will come from three primary sources:

* Bank\-referred opportunities
* Existing wealth clients
* Your own business development efforts




In partnership with wealth advisors and private client bankers, you will uncover opportunities with existing and prospective high net worth and ultra\-high net worth clients. Your focus will be generating new business. You will not have a “book” of clients or ongoing relationship management responsibilities.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Collaborate with bankers to identify and prioritize opportunities for new wealth relationships
* Engage with Wealth Advisors on deepening existing wealth relationships
* Deliver initial wealth management counsel to prospects and clients recommend customized wealth solutions and the right team to serve their needs
* Generate new assets under management through a focused sales process
* Keep abreast of trends and strategies in wealth management

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* Series 7, 63, and 65 and insurance licensed
* College graduate with 7\+ years of industry experience
* Proven ability to effectively market and sell wealth management products and services to high net worth and ultra\-high net worth clients
* A sound knowledge base of investing, trust and estates, financial planning, insurance, alternative investments, family wealth, tax considerations, and other related areas
* A self\-confident, proactive professional with the maturity necessary to work autonomously and with people of all levels in the organization
* Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills




**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* Advanced Degree Preferred
* CFP or CFA designation a plus

Ghassemian Law Group

Mission Viejo, CA, US

Ghassemian Law Group is a fast\-growing, well\-respected business litigation firm in need of an executive who is passionate about growing and scaling a high quality organization. Our firm offers a competitive salary and great benefits. In this strategic position you will play a crucial role in elevating our fast\-growing firm to the next level. If you have a passion to help businesses be successful, you will be rewarded since you will make an impact everyday.

* Design and implement business strategies, plans and procedures
* Set, monitor, and achieve comprehensive goals for performance and growth
* Evaluate performance by analyzing and interpreting data and metrics
* Supervise the work of the non\-lawyer support staff and vendors
* Lead recruitment, hiring, staffing, and general human resources operations, including payroll and benefits administration
* Ensure that the firm’s business systems and processes are fully documented in writing, organized, and being followed
* Ensure clients and matters move through the workflow pipeline at the right pace
* Use financial reports to drive operational decisions

Education and Experience

**Position Title:** Senior Director of Development  
**Department:** Development  
**Classification:** Regular, Full\-Time Exempt, works from Jewish Long Beach Offices  
**Supervisor:** Chief Executive Officer  
**Salary Range:** $95,000 \- $150,000, depending on experience

*The following statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities or requirements of this position. Employees are expected to perform other functions as assigned or requested to further support the organization’s mission.*

**About the Organization**

Open to everyone, Jewish Long Beach (JLB) has served our community by improving lives, building bridges of understanding and inclusion, and building a vibrant Jewish community across three interconnected pillars (Alpert JCC, Jewish Community Foundation, and Jewish Federation) since 1948\. Each year, more than 10,000 people visit the Alpert JCC for experiences that span early childhood education, day camp, fitness, recreation and aquatics, and Jewish cultural programs. Learn more about who we are and our mission by visiting www.JewishLongBeach.org.

**Position Overview**

We are seeking our next Senior Director of Development (SDD) to help lead and expand the philanthropic vision of Jewish Long Beach.

Jewish Long Beach is on a mission to strengthen community, deepen connection, and expand opportunity across three core pillars: the Jewish Community Foundation, the Jewish Federation, and the Alpert Jewish Community Center. Together, these platforms create a dynamic ecosystem for impact, both locally and beyond.

With over $30 million in managed assets and nearly $2 million raised annually, Jewish Long Beach serves as both a steward of long\-term legacy giving and a driver of immediate community investment.

The Senior Director of Development will play a critical leadership role in growing this impact by cultivating major gifts, shaping donor strategy, and building a culture of philanthropy that sustains and advances Jewish life across our region.

This is a role that thrives at the intersection of strategy and action. You’ll be part of the senior leadership team and work side by side with the CEO to create experiences that inspire giving, foster stewardship, and grow our community. Your work will not just fund programs; it will fuel our collective mission and deepen the sense of belonging for everyone we serve.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy to support the mission of Jewish Long Beach and its Foundation
* Oversee all fundraising activities, including major gifts, annual giving, planned giving, and special events
* Ensure that all fundraising efforts comply with ethical and legal standards, as well as organization's policies and procedures
* Monitor and analyze fundraising data to measure progress towards goals and make strategic adjustments as needed
* Collaborate with marketing team and senior leadership to develop and implement effective messaging and materials for fundraising campaigns
* Lead and manage a team of philanthropy professionals, providing guidance, support, and mentorship in their fundraising efforts
* Cultivate and maintain relationships with major donors, foundations, corporations, and community partners to secure funding
* Work closely with leadership and program directors to identify funding priorities and develop compelling cases for support
* Provide regular updates and reports to leadership, the Board, and committees on fundraising progress and initiatives
* Foster a culture of philanthropy within the organization, working to educate and engage staff, volunteers, and board members in fundraising efforts
* Represent Jewish Long Beach and the Foundation in the community, serving as an ambassador and advocate for the organization
* Stay current on trends and best practices in philanthropy and fundraising, continuously seeking new and innovative ways to engage donors and raise funds
* Act as a liaison between donors and Jewish Long Beach, ensuring that their contributions are recognized and stewarded appropriately
* Collaborate with other departments within the organization to support fundraising efforts and promote a cohesive approach to philanthropy
* Lead the Foundation’s efforts to fulfill development goals and strategies, including a particular emphasis on annual goals
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward donors across JLB initiatives ensuring personal, high\-touch engagement
* Manage Foundation granting, scholarships, and legacy giving including proposals, reporting, and donor communications
* Use data and CRM tools to track relationships, campaigns, and outcomes adjusting strategies as needed

**Skills and Competencies**

* Doer and Relationship Builder: You thrive in a hands\-on role, bringing energy and \\focus to every initiative while connecting authentically with donors and stakeholders.
* Communicator Extraordinaire: You craft compelling stories and deliver them with clarity—whether in writing, in conversation, or in front of a group.
* Juggle with Grace: You navigate multiple campaigns and priorities seamlessly, keeping everything moving forward without losing sight of impact.
* Collaborator at Heart: You enjoy working with volunteers, Board members, and donors to co\-create experiences that inspire giving and engagement.
* Culturally Fluent: You understand Jewish culture, philanthropy, and the ecosystem of Federation and Foundation giving, bringing context and insight to your work.
* Learner: Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

**Education, Experience and Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree required, advanced degree preferred
* Minimum 5 years of professional fundraising, with the ideal candidate having experience in direct solicitation, legacy solicitation, and campaign execution
* Experience with Federation campaigns, major gifts, and Foundation fundr

**Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast**
=================================================

  

  

Arizona State University Foundation has partnered with Lindauer, a national search and talent firm, to conduct this search. To apply, please submit your resume on the Lindauer website .  



  

Please contact the Lindauer team leading this search if you have questions or would like to make a nomination or a referral: Adele Mezher , Senior Vice President and Emily Horsford , Senior Associate.  



  

The salary range for this role is $180,000\-230,000 annually.  



  

  

The West Coast represents one of Arizona State University's most significant opportunities for philanthropic growth and broader engagement. ASU has built a growing presence through its academic programs, students and alumni, partnerships, physical locations, and connections to industries shaping the future. The opportunity now is to translate that presence into a more powerful and sustained culture of philanthropy in the region.  



  

ASU Foundation seeks an entrepreneurial, strategic, and accomplished fundraising leader to serve as Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast. Based in California, the Executive Director will serve as a senior advancement leader for the region, building relationships with philanthropists, entrepreneurs, business and community leaders, alumni, and other partners whose interests intersect with the breadth and ambition of ASU.  



  

The Executive Director will look beyond traditional sources of higher education philanthropy to identify new networks of wealth and influence. The region’s philanthropic landscape is not monolithic; success will require a leader who understands the distinct dynamics of the region including those between Northern and Southern California, recognizes where new wealth is emerging, and knows how to build authentic relationships within those communities.  



  

This is both a frontline fundraising and leadership role. The Executive Director will personally cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio of significant donors and prospects while leading an experienced regional advancement team toward greater focus, collaboration, accountability, and philanthropic results. As momentum and philanthropic opportunity grow, the Executive Director will also have the opportunity to shape and expand the advancement operation to support ASU's ambitions across the region.

The Executive Director will translate those strengths into compelling philanthropic opportunities, connecting donor interests with the people, programs, and ideas capable of creating meaningful impact  



  

For a creative and entrepreneurial advancement leader, this is an opportunity to help shape the next chapter of ASU's presence on the West Coast and build a culture of philanthropy matching the scale of the University's ambitions.  



  

  

Reporting to the Chief Global Advancement Officer of the ASU Foundation, the Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast will lead ASUF's advancement strategy and regional team across California and the broader West Coast. The Executive Director will personally manage a significant portfolio of major and principal gift prospects while providing focused leadership, direction, and accountability to an experienced team.  



  

Working across the ASU Foundation and in close partnership with university leadership, schools, colleges, institutes, the ASU Alumni Association, Sun Devil Athletics, and other ASU entities, the Executive Director will bring coordination and strategic focus to advancement activity across the region. jobs.title: Non-Profit Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

Executive Director provides leadership and management to ensure the organization fulfills its mission. This role requires broad oversight of operations, staff supervision, program continuity, financial accountability, and community engagement.

The Executive Director partners closely with the Board of Directors to sustain organizational health and prepare for the onboarding of permanent leadership. Executive Director will work closely with the faculty, staff, and contractors to strengthen infrastructure and position the Bowen Center for long\-term success.

The Bowen Center's work is grounded in Bowen Family Systems Theory, and this role requires a leader who can operate effectively within that framework and culture. The Executive Director’s performance will be evaluated by the Board of Directors annually.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Leadership \& Administration**

* Provide mission\-aligned leadership to the organization.
* Principal decision maker on key areas of management and programming.
* Lead, manage, support, and collaborate with staff, faculty and the Board of Directors ensuring clear communication and positive work environment.
* Build operational and technical continuity and institutional memory across staffing, systems, and annual workflows.
* Implement Board policies and maintain continuity of strategic plan activities.
* Oversee daily operations and maintain efficient, effective service delivery.

**Program Development \& Implementation** 

* Ensure the continuity and quality of educational programs grounded in Bowen theory.
* Maintain program schedules, communications, and promotional materials.
* Monitor program outcomes and provide updates to the Board.
* Partner effectively with the Bowen Center's volunteer faculty who lead conferences training programs, and educational offerings.
* Support the Center's mix of online, hybrid, and in\-person programming.
* Foster faculty development and support efforts to attract and cultivate emerging and local faculty

**Financial Management**

* Efficiently manage the operating budget in collaboration with the Treasurer/Finance Committee.
* Oversee reporting, compliance, forecasting, and financial accountability.
* Maintain donor and funder relationships; ensure timely reporting obligations.
* Develop and implement strategy for fundraising, including grant opportunities.

**Community Relations \& Outreach**

* Represent the organization with funders, partners, alumni, and community stakeholders.
* Maintain relationships with collaborating organizations and networks.
* Support the organization's in\-person presence in the District, Maryland, and Virginia area.

**Board Relations \& Governance**

* Serve as primary liaison between faculty and the Board.
* Provide regular updates on finances, operations, and program status, including staffing and organizational continuity.
* Support Board committees.
* Partner effectively with the Board on organizational priorities.

**Organizational Capacity Building**

* Document systems, policies, and processes for continuity.
* Identify organizational strengths, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
* Ensures the staffing model supports a sustainable team structure.
* Support succession planning and leadership continuity for the organization over time.

**Qualifications**

* At least a master’s degree in mental health, family therapy, organizational development, or related field
* Demonstrated understanding of and commitment to Bowen Family Systems Theory.
* Minimum of 5 years of experience in nonprofit management or leadership preferred.
* Previous experience in effective fiscal management, forecasting, fundraising, and grant management and grant writing.
* Effective interpersonal and communication abilities.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and relevant digital tools.
* Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively with boards, staff, faculty, and contractors

**Personal Qualities**

* Grounded in Bowen theory for a thinking approach to leadership and problem\-solving.
* Ability to manage organizational and personal anxiety during periods of change.
* Flexible, adaptive, and collaborative leadership style.
* Commitment to continuous learning and professional growth.
* Ability to build trust across board, faculty, and staff relationships.
* Ability to balance operational execution with longer\-term organizational development.

Additional Considerations Candidates may maintain private practice or consulting work alongside the role, provided, the responsibilities of the position and the 35\-hour weekly commitment are fully met.

Benefits: The Bowen Center offers employee health and vision benefits program, EAP, professional development, and the opportunity to travel for national and international speaking opportunities.

Pay: $90,000\.00 \- $110,000\.00 per year

Application Question(s):

* Can you commit to being in the office two days a week?
* Are you willing to travel nationally and internationally to represent the center?
* The salary range is $92K–$115K. If offered, would you accept within that range?

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Arlington, VA 22201

**Job Summary**

The Managing Director, Sustainability \& Corporate Citizenship provides enterprise leadership for AEP's sustainability strategy, disclosure governance, stakeholder engagement, and philanthropic initiatives. The role is responsible for advancing AEP's reputation, strengthening stakeholder trust, supporting access to capital, and ensuring transparency through high\-quality sustainability disclosures and strategic community investments.  

This leader will oversee the AEP Foundation, corporate charitable giving programs, volunteerism, sustainability reporting, ESG investor engagement, disclosure governance, and related data management processes. The position serves as a key advisor to executive leadership and the Board of Directors on sustainability and emerging stakeholder expectations.  

The Managing Director works across operating companies, Investor Relations, Finance, Legal, Corporate Communications, Regulatory Affairs, and External Affairs to ensure alignment between AEP's business strategy, sustainability priorities, and philanthropic initiatives.**Job Description**

**Sustainability Strategy, Governance \& Disclosure**
-----------------------------------------------------

* Lead the development, execution, and continuous improvement of AEP's enterprise sustainability strategy and associated governance framework.
* Own AEP's sustainability disclosure program, including the annual AEP Impact Report and related external sustainability reporting.
* Establish and maintain enterprise processes, controls, technology platforms, and governance structures supporting sustainability and non\-financial disclosures.
* Lead the collection, validation, management, and governance of sustainability\-related data and metrics across the enterprise.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
Eastside Academy is creating a Director of Operations role for the first time as a deliberate investment in our organizational capacity and future. Until now, many of these responsibilities have been carried by the Executive Director alongside broader executive leadership responsibilities. This new role brings them together under a dedicated leader who can strengthen the systems, people, and infrastructure supporting the entire organization. The Director will join organizational leadership, lead an existing Operations Team, and build an operating environment in which people have the clarity, information, and support they need to do their best work.


### **About Eastside Academy**


Education is more than a basic right – it's essential to our ability to thrive. However, life's challenges can often stand in the way through no fault of our own. We believe that every student deserves access to holistic and wraparound care. Eastside Academy was created as a refuge and place of growth for high school students who may not fit the mold of traditional schools. We are different by design. Our unique and innovative approach to student life reaches beyond traditional education models. We provide an individualized education plan and holistic counseling to all students. Through our housing program, we can provide a safe and stable home environment for students with greater needs.
### **Description**


**Director of Operations**
==========================

**Location:** Bellevue, Washington

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Status:** Full\-time, exempt

**Salary:** $100,000–$115,000 annually

**Build the systems that allow a mission to flourish**
======================================================


Eastside Academy is creating a Director of Operations role for the first time as a deliberate investment in our organizational capacity and future.


Until now, many of these responsibilities have been carried by the Executive Director alongside broader executive leadership responsibilities. This new role brings them together under a dedicated leader who can strengthen the systems, people, and infrastructure supporting the entire organization.


The Director will join organizational leadership, lead an existing Operations Team, and build an operating environment in which people have the clarity, information, and support they need to do their best work.

**About Eastside Academy**
==========================


Eastside Academy is a nonprofit alternative high school and support program in Bellevue, Washington. Our mission is to inspire change in the lives of youth through high school education, counseling, recovery, housing, and life skills in a Christ\-centered environment.


Our students often come to Eastside Academy after not finding meaning, value, or success in traditional school settings. We walk alongside students and families through an integrated model of education, mental health care, and relational support that helps young people rediscover hope, purpose, and the possibility of a different future.

**What winning looks like**
===========================


The Director of Operations creates an organization in which the systems supporting the mission are dependable, visible, appropriately owned, and increasingly proactive. Staff spend less energy navigating operational friction, leaders have trustworthy information, risks are addressed early, and organizational growth does not require proportional increases in complexity.


Success means that:

  

* Facilities, technology, vendors, and administrative systems function reliably.
* Financial processes are accurate, timely, and well controlled.
* Employees experience clear and dependable people systems.
* Risks, compliance requirements, and recurring deadlines are addressed proactively.
* The Operations Team demonstrates increasing ownership and effectiveness.
* Routine operational matters no longer require the Executive Director’s involvement.
* EA’s systems become more scalable and less dependent on individual staff knowledge.

**What you will lead**
======================

### **Organizational Operations \+ Infrastructure**


Build and improve organization\-wide workflows, calendars, facilities, technology, purchasing, vendor relationships, and administrative systems. Clarify ownership, coordinate cross\-functional handoffs, remove operational friction, and lead Operations\-owned logistics for major organizational events and transitions.

### **Financial Operations \+ Stewardship**


Lead the Office Manager \+ Financial Administrator and oversee reliable financial\-administration systems. Partner with external accounting professionals, strengthen internal controls, monitor spending, support budgeting and forecasting, and provide leaders with trustworthy financial information for decision\-making.

### **People Operations \+ Organizational Support**


Coordinate HR administration, onboarding, offboarding, benefits, personnel documentation, required training, policies, and recurring employment processes. Build dependable systems that support employees and supervisors while department leaders retain authority for hiring, supervision, performance management, and personnel decisions within their teams.

### **Risk, Compliance, \+ Organizational Readiness**


Maintain organization\-wide compliance calendars, documentation, renewals, records, safety planning, and emergency\-readiness systems. Coordinate timelines and approvals across departments while functional leaders retain responsibility for the accuracy and submission of reporting from their areas.

### **Operations Team Leadership \+ Organizational Capacity**


Lead, coach, and develop the Office Manager \+ Financial Administrator and Manager of Community Engagement. Establish clear priorities, decision rights, accountability, and sustainable workloads. Executive Director  
Tupper Arts, Inc. — Tupper Lake, NY  
Tupper Arts, Inc. is seeking an experienced, community\-minded Executive Director to lead our multi\-disciplinary arts center in the heart of the Adirondacks. This is a rare opportunity to shape the cultural life of a small rural region — overseeing a vibrant visual and performing arts program.  
Position Overview  
The Executive Director provides strategic, operational, and financial leadership for the organization, working closely with the Board of Directors to advance Tupper Arts' mission. The ED oversees a small but dedicated team, and serves as the organization's chief representative to donors, community partners, and the public. This new position will take a lead role in the oversight of a major renovation of a theater, including management of state and private grants.

Duties

Operations \& Administration

* Oversee day\-to\-day organizational operations including facilities, technology, human resources and vendor relationships
* Build and maintain administrative systems appropriate for the organization; ordering goods and services, building maintenance scheduling, tracking attendance of visitorsLeadership \& Strategy
* Partner with the Board to develop and implement a multi\-year strategic plan aligned with the organization’s mission and financial reality with short and long term goals and metrics
* Be the primary face of the organization to donors, funders, municipal partners, media, local businesses, and the arts community.
* Foster a positive, inclusive organizational culture that attracts and retains talented staff
* Prepare for and present operational reports at all board meetings; support board recruitment, orientation, and committee work

Fundraising \& Development

* Maintain and grow relationships with foundations; oversee grant writing and reporting (with staff or contracted support)

* Monitor financial performance across across all program areas (gallery, classes, theater, live performances, special events); ensure accurate and timely reporting on cost analysis of each area
* Ensure compliance with all nonprofit financial, legal, and regulatory requirements including annual audit
* Ensure system is put in place to pay invoices and submit reimbursement requests to grant sources in a timely manner
* Oversee the administration of all grants and contracts

* Demonstrated success in fundraising, grant writing, and/or donor relations
* Experience managing staff and volunteers

The Executive Director serves as a primary point of contact for members, prospective members, sponsors, vendors, and the public and is expected to represent the Association in a professional and responsive manner.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

Neighborhood Housing Services of South Florida (NHSSF) seeks an experienced, strategic, and growth\-oriented President \& Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the organization into its next chapter. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the President \& CEO will provide overall leadership and be responsible for strategic direction, financial sustainability, operational effectiveness, program performance, and organizational growth.

NHSSF is seeking an entrepreneurial leader who can strengthen current operations while identifying new opportunities for growth. A key priority will be diversifying revenue through new funding sources, strategic partnerships, earned\-income opportunities, lending\-related revenue, and other sustainable sources. The President \& CEO will also evaluate existing programs, identify opportunities to improve or expand services, and develop new initiatives that respond to community needs and market opportunities.

The ideal candidate will have significant nonprofit or mission\-driven leadership experience, preferably in housing, community and economic development, lending, financial services, real estate, or related sectors. Knowledge of the South Florida housing and/or finance market, particularly Miami\-Dade and Broward Counties, and established regional relationships are highly desirable.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and establish a clear vision for NHSSF’s growth, impact, and long\-term sustainability.
* Work with the Board of Directors to develop and implement strategic and financial priorities.
* Strengthen operational systems, financial management, accountability, and organizational performance.
* Develop and execute strategies to diversify and increase revenue, including grants, governmentcontracts, corporate and philanthropic support, strategic partnerships, earned income, and lending\-related opportunities.
* Review and analyze existing programs for effectiveness, community impact, financial viability, and alignment with NHSSF’s mission.
* Identify and develop new programs, services, and business opportunities that support organizational growth and respond to community needs.
* Establish measurable financial, operational, and programmatic performance goals.
* Evaluate staffing and organizational structure to ensure NHSSF has the capacity to achieve its goals.
* Build and expand relationships with government agencies, financial institutions, funders, developers,philanthropic organizations, and community partners.
* Serve as a visible ambassador for NHSSF throughout South Florida and within the housing, community development, and financial sectors.
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and high performance.

**Governance \& Reporting**

The President \& CEO will report directly to the NHSSF Board of Directors, with the Board Chair serving as the primary liaison. The President \& CEO will oversee the day\-to\-day management of the organization and provide regular updates to the Board regarding financial performance, programs, operations, strategic initiatives, and organizational growth.

The President \& CEO will collaborate with NHSSF staff, the Lending Consultant, outsourced CFO, and other professional advisors to ensure alignment among lending activities, financial management, programs, and organizational priorities.

**Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10 years of senior management or executive leadership experience in a nonprofit,housing, community development, financial services, lending, real estate, economic development, orrelated organization.
* Demonstrated experience leading organizational growth, transition, restructuring, or improvement.
* Proven success developing new and diversified revenue streams and strategic partnerships.
* Experience evaluating existing programs and developing new programs, services, or business opportunities.
* Strong financial and operational management skills, including budgeting, cash flow management, financial controls, forecasting, and organizational planning.
* Experience working effectively with Boards of Directors, funders, government agencies, financial institutions, and community stakeholders.
* Experience in affordable housing, homeownership, community development, lending, financial capability, or related sectors strongly preferred.
* Knowledge of the South Florida housing, real estate, community development, and/or financial markets strongly preferred; established relationships in Miami\-Dade and Broward Counties are highly desirable.
* Entrepreneurial and results\-oriented leadership style with strong communication, relationship\-building, consensus\-building, and team\-development skills.
* Strong commitment to NHSSF’s mission and to expanding housing and economic opportunities throughout South Florida.

**Compensation**

NHSSF offers a competitive compensation package commensurate with experience and qualifications.

**About NHSSF**

Neighborhood Housing Services of South Florida is committed to strengthening communities and expanding housing and economic opportunities for individuals and families throughout South Florida. Through its programs, partnerships, lending activities, and community development efforts, NHSSF works to create pathways to housing stability, homeownership, financial capability, and stronger neighborhoods.

Pay: $90,000\.00 \- $120,000\.00 per year

**About Healthy Community Alliance**

Healthy Community Alliance, Inc. (HCA) is a nonprofit organization based in Gowanda, New York, serving Cattaraugus County, Chautauqua County, and portions of Erie and Wyoming counties. Founded in 1996, HCA is one of 30 rural health networks supported by the New York State Department of Health’s Charles D. Cook Office of Rural Health. HCA’s mission is to enhance quality of life in rural communities through inclusive partnerships that promote wellness and prevention. HCA provides both direct services and regional support, with programs focused on health access, caregiver and senior services, maternal and infant health, insurance navigation, nutrition, and more. The organization also builds regional capacity through fiscal sponsorship, administrative support, and network coordination. A key feature of HCA’s work is its ownership of a multi\-use facility in Gowanda. Upper floors house Academy Place Apartments, HUD\-supported senior housing, a limited partnership governed by the Academy Place Housing Development Fund Company (“Academy Place”). Community Place LLC, a subsidiary of HCA located on the first floor, serves as a commercial hub for medical, behavioral health, aging services, recreation, and food access. **Mission, Vision, and Values** 

The Nashville Food Project brings people together to grow, cook, and share nourishing food, with the goals of cultivating community and alleviating hunger in our city. At The Nashville Food Project, we embrace a vision of vibrant community food security in which everyone in Nashville has access to the food they want and need through a just and sustainable food system. This mission and vision are guided by core organizational values, including hospitality, stewardship, interdependence, learning, justice, and transformation.

**Organizational Background** 

The Nashville Food Project (TNFP) was born from the idea that good food is a matter of basic dignity. Since its start in 2007, TNFP has served thousands of Nashvillians facing food insecurity. In 2011, TNFP was incorporated as an independent nonprofit, shifting the focus of its meals program toward a collaborative partnership model and launching an urban agriculture program. Today, TNFP continues to connect people to nourishing food and to each other through vibrant urban agriculture projects, made\-from\-scratch meals, and food shared with local partners working to disrupt cycles of poverty.

**Position Summary** 

The Senior Director of Community Engagement (SDCE) leads TNFP's community engagement programs, which include community agriculture, volunteerism, and education. jobs.title: Senior Vice President & Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Who is the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra?**  

Known for its artistic excellence for more than 130 years, today the PSO is the region’s national and international cultural ambassador. A two\-time 2018 GRAMMY® Award\-winning orchestral ensemble credited with a rich history of concerts, performances, and recordings with the world’s finest conductors and musicians, the PSO consistently demonstrates a genuine commitment to Pittsburgh’s citizens, regional communities, and vibrant cultural scene. The internationally acclaimed Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra (PSO) engages audiences of all ages through unparalleled live musical experiences, community collaborations, and educational programming that enrich every life with great music.  

  

**JOB PURPOSE AND REPORTING STRUCTURE:**  

The Senior Vice President \& Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a key strategic and operational partner with the CEO and other organizational leadership in decision making and fulfilling the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra’s mission and goals. The COO is responsible for executing on annual and long\-term plans of the PSO through leadership and supervision in the following areas: artistic planning, strategic planning, orchestra\-, stage\-, and facility\-operations, electronic media, technology, orchestra personnel, labor relations, community programs, business intelligence, and general operations. The COO is part of the senior leadership team and works closely with the CEO, the CFO, the CDO, the CREO, the Music Director, the Board of Directors and other members of the leadership team on the execution of mission and strategic direction of the organization.  

  

**Direct Reports:** Vice President of Artistic Planning, Vice President of Operations, Vice President of Information Technology, Senior Vice President of Learning \& Engagement, Director of Commercial \& Popular Programming and Executive Administrative Associate.  

  

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES:**  

Leadership – the COO provides organizational leadership with a focus on daily internal operations as well as partnering with the C\-Suite on strategic planning for the future. The COO provides organizational leadership in the CEO’s absence and is the public face of the organization in the CEO’s absence. The COO provides general oversight of the PSI’s management operating system to ensure that planning processes, management controls, and internal communications effectively deliver the business of the PSI.  

  

Span of Control \- the COO supervises and directs all departments responsible for planning, developing and executing the Symphony seasons, Heinz Hall programming and operations, as well as activities related to education, electronic media and community programs. They work closely with the CFO and CEO on budget development and monitoring as well as long\-range financial planning for operational expenses. The COO also works in conjunction with senior leadership on the development and execution of the strategic plan, community projects, community relationships, run out and tour relationships as well as fundraising and marketing and communications when appropriate.  

  

Capital Projects \- The COO provides executive leadership and oversight for the PSO’s capital projects, ensuring investment strategies align with corporate objectives, operational priorities, growth initiatives, and long\-term financial goals. Direct capital planning and resource allocation processes across departments to maximize return and support sustainable organizational growth. Partner with executive leadership and key stakeholders to develop business cases, assess risks, establish funding priorities, and make strategic decisions regarding major capital investments.  

  

Staff Development and Management – The COO is responsible for ensuring that the departments are staffed appropriately and within the financial forecasts. The COO ensures that performance expectations are clearly defined, measured and if needed addressed. The COO, in conjunction with department leadership, identifies opportunities for employee growth and training. The COO leads the efforts to ensure that the work environment allows staff to perform, thrive and succeed.  

  

Labor Relations – The COO, in conjunction with the CEO, CFO, CREO and VP of Operations, is responsible for the labor relations management on behalf of the Symphony and for developing and maintaining collaborative working relationships with the labor unions working within the organization. This includes working closely with the VP of Operations and CREO on regular contract management, grievance processes and the collective bargaining negotiations process with seven unions. The COO ensures that the collective bargaining processes are aligned with the organizational direction strategies and goals. The COO also works with the CEO, VP of Operations and Director of Orchestra Personnel on individual contract negotiations with PSO musicians.  

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:*** College degree required, advanced degree and musical background preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of increasing responsibility in operational leadership and strategic planning.
* At least 8 years of experience in arts management, preferably in orchestra management.
* At least 5 years of experience in a senior management role with a professional arts organization.
* Demonstrated experience in motivating, managing and developing teams.
* Experience with large capital projects.
* Experience with labor negotiations and collective bargaining agreements.
* Working knowledge of orchestra repertoire and orchestra operations.

**Compensation and Location:**  

This is a full\-time exempt position with an annual salary between $200,000 \- $270,000 depending upon experience. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes paid holidays, paid time off, employer paid health benefits, as well as retirement savings options with an employer match.
