jobs.title: Executive Director, Chief Operations Officer - Aetna Better Health of Maryland
jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

**Position Summary**


Aetna Better Health is Aetna’s Medicaid managed care plan. Backed by over 30 years of experience managing the care of those with a broad array of health care needs, our Medicaid plans have demonstrated that getting the right help when you need it is essential to better health. That’s why Aetna® Medicaid plans include the guidance and support needed to connect our members with the right coverage, resources, and care. We are focused on enhancing quality and population health outcomes while integrating CVS assets to bring accessible healthcare to our members.

  

Aetna Better Health of Maryland is seeking an experience leader with vast operational knowledge of Medicaid for its state\-wide managed Medicaid business in the role of Chief Operations Officer (COO). The COO role will be strategic and committed to developing colleagues as well as relentlessly pursuing change that is best for the organization and its customers. The COO role will collaborate with the CEO to develop the strategic vision of the Health Plan, policies \& procedures, and operational objectives including leading RFP readiness efforts. The COO will oversee high level strategic and operational activities of various plan functional areas which include traditional service operations (Claims, Provider Services, Information Technology, Grievance \& Appeals and Member Services) as well as Medical Management (Quality, Network, Compliance, Health Equity, Medical Directors, Utilization Management, Vendor Management). These activities may include colleague productivity, building and maintaining a highly inclusive and diverse culture as well as ensuring team members thrive and organizational outcomes are met.

 **Major Responsibilities**

* Partner with the Plan CEO to drive successful growth, operational excellence, and overall business performance.
* Oversee financial management of the health plan, including budget accountability, revenue target achievement, and P\&L performance.
* Collaborate with corporate functional leaders and centralized shared services teams to drive operational effectiveness and business results.
* Provide leadership and oversight across core operational areas, including: Claims systems and processing, Third\-Party Liability (TPL) and Coordination of Benefits (COB), Pharmacy claims operations and their impact on total cost of care, Call center operations and performance and Encounter data management and processing.
* Lead and support provider operations activities, including: Provider data management, Credentialing, Provider relations, Network development and contracting, and Value\-based care contracting and performance initiatives.
* Drive strategies that enhance provider experience while managing medical costs and improving operational outcomes.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable state contracts, regulations, executive orders, and healthcare industry requirements.
* Partner with Government Affairs and Legal teams to address regulatory, legislative, and compliance\-related matters.
* Serve as a key advocate with internal stakeholders, state regulators, policymakers, and other external partners.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with community\-based advocacy organizations and industry stakeholders.
* Oversee communications and engagement strategies for members and providers.
* Support and promote community\-based programs that address Social Determinants of Health (SDOH), including housing, employment, Community Health Workers (CHWs), Peer support specialists and nutrition and food access initiatives.
* Apply expertise in the integration of physical and behavioral healthcare, with a strong understanding of the unique needs of the Medicaid population.
* Represent the organization externally with regulatory agencies, state departments, community partners, and other key stakeholders.
* Act as a trusted executive leader and extension of the CEO, providing strategic leadership both internally and externally.

  

The COO will oversee business operations performance and employee productivity, building and maintaining our highly inclusive and diverse culture, ensuring team members thrive, and organizational outcomes are met. Lead people, build/maintain relationships while driving talent and culture development.

 **Required Qualifications**


The candidate will have a strong work ethic, be a self\-starter, and be able to be highly productive in a dynamic, collaborative environment. This position offers broad exposure to all aspects of the company’s business, as well as significant interaction with all the business leaders. The candidate will be expected to have the following key attributes:

  

* 10\+ years of work experience reflecting a proven track record of government programs such as Medicaid, Medicare, or Dual Eligible plans.
* 5\+ years of experience in executive leadership roles with proven track record of proficiency in the operational competencies noted.
* Demonstrated success with C\-suite stakeholders.
* Ability to work collaboratively across many teams, prioritize demands from those teams, synthesize information received, and generate meaningful conclusions.
* Ability to conceive innovative ideas or solutions to meet clients’ requirements.
* Excellent communication and relationship management skills and being able to express thoughts in an organized and articulate manner.
* Ability to build a climate of trust and respect with regulators, external stakeholders, as well as colleagues, peers, and our internal growth partners.
* Pr

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**Director of Development**


Phoenixville, PA

 **﻿Lead fundraising initiatives that create measurable community impact, strengthen donor relationships, and help our mission reach more people each year.**

 **Why You'll Love Working with Us**

* **Drive Meaningful Impact:** Help expand programs that empower individuals and families to move from crisis to stability throughout Lancaster and Chester Counties.
* **Build Lasting Relationships:** Cultivate meaningful connections with donors, community partners, and advocates whose generosity directly changes lives.
* **Shape Our Future:** Help guide the continued growth of a respected nonprofit organization.
* **Join a Supportive Team:** Collaborate with compassionate colleagues who celebrate one another, value teamwork, and are united by a shared commitment to serving the community.
* **Enjoy the Best of Both Worlds:** Bring your energy, passion, and development expertise to a growing organization where you can make a significant impact without the layers and stress often found in larger nonprofits.
* **Grow Your Career:** Take on a highly visible leadership role where your ideas, initiative, and fundraising expertise will make a lasting organizational impact while advancing your professional growth.

 **About Us**


Good Samaritan Services compassionately responds to individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness across Lancaster and Chester Counties, walking alongside our neighbors as they move from crisis to stability through outreach, housing, and ongoing support. We believe lasting change happens through meaningful relationships, collaboration, and responsible stewardship, and we're committed to growing our impact so we can serve more people throughout the communities we call home.

 **What You'll Do as Our Director of Development**

* **Lead** annual fundraising initiatives, campaigns, special events, and development projects that advance our mission and achieve annual revenue goals.
* **Cultivate** and grow a portfolio of individual donors while identifying and engaging prospective major donors who are passionate about expanding our community impact.
* **Strengthen** donor relationships through thoughtful stewardship, personalized communication, and meaningful engagement that inspires long\-term support.
* **Represent** Good Samaritan Services at community events, donor meetings, presentations, and partnership opportunities, serving as a trusted ambassador for our mission.
* **Support** our upcoming transformational capital campaign by coordinating fundraising efforts, engaging donors, and helping drive campaign success.
* **Collaborate** with our Chief Advancement Officer and a talented team of development, marketing, grant writing, and engagement professionals to align fundraising strategies with organizational priorities.
* **Champion** our culture of compassion, collaboration, stewardship, and accountability while contributing to organization\-wide initiatives that strengthen our impact throughout the communities we serve.

 **Our Ideal Director of Development**

* **Mission\-Driven:** You're inspired by serving others and are motivated by the opportunity to make a lasting difference in the lives of individuals and families experiencing homelessness.
* **Relationship Builder:** You naturally earn trust, cultivate meaningful donor and community relationships, and inspire others to invest in a shared mission.
* **Experienced Fundraiser:** Five plus years of progressive nonprofit development experience with a proven record of securing major gifts, growing donor portfolios, leading successful fundraising events, and delivering engaging public presentations.
* **Strategic Self\-Starter:** You take initiative, stay organized, adapt to changing priorities, and confidently manage multiple projects while maintaining a high standard of accountability.
* **Qualified Professional:** You hold a bachelor's degree, work independently while holding yourself to a high standard of accountability, thrive when trusted and given room to run, and confidently read a room to build meaningful relationships and respond with professionalism and emotional intelligence.
* **Collaborative Team Member:** You thrive in a supportive, mission\-driven environment, value teamwork, and contribute to a culture built on compassion, stewardship, generosity, partnership, and shared success.

 **What We Offer Our Director of Development**

* Compensation: $75,000\-$90,000 annually, DOE
* Health Insurance
* Dental \& Vision Insurance
* Paid Time Off
* Paid Holidays
* Retirement Plan with a 3% employer match.
* Disability Insurance
* Mileage Reimbursement
* Company Laptop
* Authentic Community: Be part of a supportive culture where employees celebrate one another's successes, encourage personal and professional growth, and work alongside colleagues whose own life experiences reflect the lasting impact of our mission.

 **To Apply**


Director of Development, Nonprofit Development Director, Fundraising Director, Development Manager, Major Gifts Officer, and nonprofit fundraising professionals seeking a collaborative, mission\-driven organization where they can build donor relationships, lead strategic fundraising initiatives, and create lasting community impact are encouraged to explore this opportunity with Good Samaritan Services.

 *By submitting this application, you agree to receive recurring informational text messages (e.g., appointment alerts) that may be automated to the mobile number you provided at opt\-in from Team Builder Recruiting, LLC. Msg frequency may vary. Msg \& data rates may apply. Reply HELP for help and STOP to cancel. See Terms and Conditions \& Privacy Policy.*

  

Requirements:
  

* Five\+ years of progressive nonprofit development experience
* Experience with securing major gifts, growing donor portfolios, leading successful fundraising events, and delivering engaging public presentations
* Bachelor's degree required

jobs.title: Turbo Tim's Chief Operating Officer / Integrator
jobs.description:
**Chief Operating Officer / Integrator**

**Turbo Tim’s Anything Automotive \| Twin Cities, Minnesota \| Compensation: $200,000–$300,000**

Turbo Tim’s is growing, and we need a COO who can help turn big ideas into a great company at scale.

I’m Turbo Tim. In EOS and *Rocket Fuel* terms, I’m the textbook Visionary. I see possibilities everywhere, move fast, and love trying things the automotive industry hasn’t tried. I need a true Integrator beside me: someone who loves people, brings clarity to complexity, makes decisions, builds strong leaders, and turns ideas into results. You’ll be empowered to lead the business and tell me when an idea needs a better plan.

We’re an independent, multi\-location automotive company built around **Cars, Cats, and Community**. We’re expanding quickly, building a YouTube channel that shows what shop life can be, and developing a software company aimed at improving this industry. Depending on your strengths and interests, you could help shape those ventures too. We put on community events like **Car Extravaganza** and **Crushawhirl**, and our team volunteers because giving back is part of who we are. There’s a lot happening here, and the right person will help us grow it without losing what makes it special.

Our values are **Care, CommUNITY, Trust, Innovation, and FUN**. They have to show up in how we treat customers, develop employees, solve problems, and make decisions. We take employee feedback seriously: we track eNPS, listen to what drives it, and keep changing how we work to make this a better place for our people.

**What you’ll own**

* Lead day\-to\-day operations across our locations and help build the systems, accountability, and leadership capacity needed for continued growth.
* Be the Integrator: turn vision into priorities, align the leadership team, follow through, and help us decide what deserves our attention now.
* Coach and grow our leaders. Build a company where people know what success looks like and have the support to reach it.
* Own operational performance and work with the team to improve the customer experience, financial results, and execution across the business.
* Use EOS tools and a healthy leadership cadence to surface issues, make decisions, and keep us moving.
* Protect and strengthen our culture as we add people, locations, and new ventures.

**You might be our person if**

* You’ve led people and operations through meaningful growth, and you can balance big\-picture thinking with consistent follow\-through.
* You understand EOS and the Visionary/Integrator relationship in *Rocket Fuel*, ideally because you’ve lived it.
* You’re direct, kind, calm under pressure, and genuinely good at getting the best out of people.
* You can challenge a passionate founder, earn trust across a team, and make ambitious ideas executable.
* You’re excited to bring a fresh perspective to automotive. **Experience outside the automotive industry is especially welcome.**
* You care about culture and employee feedback as much as you care about a scorecard.

Our previous COO has been an amazing Integrator and person. He set a high bar. At times we wondered how we could possibly offer him more room to grow, and he kept growing anyway. Those are big shoes to fill. You won’t be expected to fill them alone: we’ll support your development, give you room to lead, and expect you to invest just as deeply in the growth of our people.

If you want to lead a company that’s growing fast, trying new things, and doing real good in the community, we’d love to meet you. **Apply with your résumé and a short note about why the Visionary/Integrator partnership appeals to you.**

Pay: $200,000\.00 \- $275,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Overview**

The Executive Director serves as the chief administrative officer for the Meadville Area Recreational Authority, providing leadership and strategic direction for the community’s recreational facilities (George S. DeArment Ice Arena, George J. Barco Aquatic Center, Lincoln Avenue Sports Complex, Watson Family Tennis Center, and Eldred Glen Baseball Field), programs, and natural assets. This role is responsible for the overall management of operations, financial sustainability, long\-range planning, and community engagement. The Executive Director ensures that the Authority provides high\-quality, inclusive, and safe recreational opportunities that enhance the quality of life for all residents of the City of Meadville, Vernon Township, and West Mead Township.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Strategic Leadership \& Governance***

* Collaborate with the Board of Directors to develop and implement a comprehensive master plan and long\-term strategic goals.
* Act as the primary liaison between the Board, local government officials, and the public.
* Ensure compliance with all local, state, and federal regulations and safety standards.
* Acts as primary contact for Human Resources issues in coordination with staff from the City of Meadville.

***Financial Management \& Development***

* Oversee the development and management of the annual operating and capital budgets.
* Identify and secure alternative funding sources, corporate sponsorships, and private donations.
* Monitor financial performance to ensure the Authority remains fiscally sound and transparent.
* Supervise and/or administer Accounts Payable, cash management, and bank deposits in coordination with staff from the City of Meadville.

**Specialized Facility Responsibilities**

***Ice Arena \& Hockey Operations***

* Oversee the technical operations of the Ice Arena, including refrigeration systems, air quality monitoring, and ice resurfacing protocols.
* Coordinate to balance ice time for youth hockey, figure skating, and public skating sessions and to maximize income.

***Aquatic Center Management***

* Supervision of Aquatics Director to ensure the completion of the following:

o Supervise the recruitment, training, and certification of lifeguards, swimming instructors, and fitness instructors.

o Develop sustainable programming for the pool, ranging from competitive swim meets to fitness and wellness classes.

* Supervision of Certified Pool Operator(s) to ensure the following:

o Direct the operations of the Aquatic Center,

o Health Regulations and Water Chemistry Monitoring: Ensure strict adherence to health department regulations regarding water chemistry, filtration, and swimmer safety. Tests and adjusts chlorine, pH, and alkalinity levels to prevent illness.

o Equipment Maintenance: Works cooperatively with the Maintenance Director to keep pumps, filters, and chemical feed systems running properly.

o Safety and Compliance: Follows local, state, and federal health codes to keep swimmers safe.

o Recordkeeping: Documents daily chemical readings and maintenance tasks

***Outdoor \& Community Assets***

* Manage specialized turf maintenance and rental agreements for the Eldred Glen Baseball Field and Lincoln Avenue Sports Complex Softball Leagues.
* Oversee the logistics for community events and facility rentals.

***Operations \& Facility Management***

* Basic understanding of HVAC, Plumbing and Electrical required for the operation of facilities in order to communicate effectively with maintenance staff and outside contractors.
* Supervision of the Maintenance Director to ensure uptime of pool and rink through completion of:

o Cleaning and sanitization of high traffic areas, restrooms and locker rooms daily and as needed to ensure a positive and healthy patron experience.

o Cleaning of low traffic areas as needed.

o Scheduled maintenance of equipment per manufacturer guidelines.

o Troubleshooting to avoid potential breakdowns.

o Planning for capital improvements.

* Direct the maintenance, improvement, and security of all recreational sites (e.g., tennis courts, pavilions, sports complexes, trails, skate park).
* Supervise the scheduling and execution of diverse recreational programming and community events.
* Oversight of outside contractors to ensure work is completed satisfactorily and in accordance with project scope.
* Negotiate and manage contracts with vendors, contractors, and service providers.

***Team Leadership***

* Recruit, mentor, and evaluate staff and volunteers.
* Foster a culture of customer service excellence, safety, and professional development.

***Community \& Public Relations***

* Serve as the "face" of the Authority, promoting its mission through public speaking, social media, and local media outlets.
* Build strong partnerships with schools, non\-profits, and local businesses to expand program reach.
* Advocate for the benefits of recreation and open space at public hearings and community meetings.

**Qualifications**

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Recreation Administration, Public Administration, Business Management, or a related field.

Experience: Leadership experience in parks and recreation or public sector management.

**Skills:**

* Proven ability in grant writing and fund development.
* Strong financial literacy and experience managing public funds.
* Excellent communication and conflict\-resolution skills.
* Proficiency in modern recreational management software and digital marketing.

**Work Environment**

This position requires a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends for board meetings and community events. Physical presence at various recreational sites is required, including outdoor environments in varying weather conditions.

Pay: $45,000\.00 \- $55,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Chamber Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Chamber of Commerce is seeking a dynamic, relationship\-focused Executive Director to serve as the organization's chief executive officer and public face. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director provides strategic leadership, oversees daily operations and financial performance, strengthens membership, develops community partnerships, and advocates for a thriving local business community.

The ideal candidate demonstrates integrity, business acumen, financial stewardship, collaboration, innovation, sound judgment, and a strong commitment to member service and results in positioning the Chamber for continued growth and long\-term sustainability.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and implement the Chamber's strategic priorities in partnership with the Board of Directors.
* Develop strategies to recruit, retain, and engage members while ensuring members recognize the value of Chamber participation.
* Manage the Chamber's budget, financial performance, resources, and revenue\-generating activities, including sponsorships, grants, fundraising, and partnerships.
* Serve as a visible community leader and Chamber spokesperson, building relationships with businesses, elected officials, government agencies, community organizations, and regional partners.
* Monitor legislative and regulatory issues and support advocacy efforts that promote business growth and economic vitality.
* Oversee Chamber communications, marketing, social media, public relations, and brand visibility.
* Provide leadership and oversight for networking events, educational programs, ribbon cuttings, awards, legislative forums, and community events.
* Serve as the principal advisor to the Board of Directors and support effective governance, committees, and volunteer leadership.
* Direct day\-to\-day operations and recruit, supervise, coach, and develop staff and volunteers.
* Build strategic partnerships and identify new opportunities that strengthen Chamber programs, services, revenue, and community impact.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Communications, Marketing, Nonprofit Management, Economic Development, or a related field or equivalent experience.
* Minimum of five years of progressively responsible leadership experience.
* Experience with nonprofit organizations, chambers of commerce, business associations, economic development, or similar organizations preferred.
* Demonstrated experience with boards of directors, budgeting, financial management, staff supervision, and organizational leadership.
* Experience in membership development, fundraising, sponsorship development, business development, or sales preferred.

jobs.description:
The University of Iowa Center for Advancement (UICA) seeks an accomplished and forward\-thinking development leader to guide fundraising strategy and performance across the University of Iowa's Main Campus. Reporting to the Senior Vice President for Development, the Vice President serves as the senior fundraising leader for Main Campus Development and chief development officer for the Office of the Provost. Through a team of senior fundraising leaders, the Vice President provides leadership and oversight for a large and complex development enterprise that includes principal gifts, regional major gifts, the University's creative campus, seven academic colleges, and a broad portfolio of university\-wide priorities, strategic initiatives, and campus units.



The Vice President establishes strategic direction, advances fundraising performance, and drives philanthropic support for the university's highest priorities across Main Campus. The Vice President works in close partnership with the Vice President for Health Sciences Development, who leads fundraising for the university's health sciences colleges and University of Iowa Health Care, to align strategy and operations, advance shared institutional priorities, and promote a coordinated, enterprise\-wide approach to philanthropy across UICA.



The successful candidate will be an accomplished fundraising leader with experience leading leaders, building high\-performing teams, securing significant philanthropic investments, and navigating complex organizations. The ideal candidate will possess exceptional relationship\-building skills, strategic judgment, political acumen, and a demonstrated ability to collaborate with senior university leaders to translate institutional priorities and strategic initiatives into philanthropic opportunities and fundraising success.


*\*\*This position is eligible for hybrid work (telecommuting), which includes working on\-site at least 3 days a week at our office in Iowa City.\*\**


*\*\*Required: Please submit a cover letter with application\*\**


**RESPONSIBILITIES**


**Strategic and Organizational Leadership**


* Provides strategic leadership and oversight for all Main Campus fundraising programs, ensuring alignment with institutional priorities and opportunities.
* Leads and develops a team of senior fundraising leaders, providing strategic guidance, coaching, and support in the development and execution of fundraising plans.
* Serves as chief development officer for the Office of the Provost and a trusted partner on matters related to engagement, philanthropy, and the advancement of university priorities.
* Contributes to UICA strategic planning and, in partnership with the Senior Vice President for Development and university leadership, to philanthropic strategies supporting university\-wide priorities and strategic initiatives.
* Collaborates with Data Analytics and advancement partners to strengthen organizational fundraising capacity and inform strategic decision\-making.
* Champions organizational change, continuous improvement, innovation, alignment, and shared accountability across multiple fundraising teams.

  


**Fundraising and Donor Engagement**


* Maintains a small portfolio of active principal and major gift prospects and is responsible for securing significant philanthropic investments in support of institutional priorities.
* Partners with senior fundraising colleagues and university leaders to develop strategies for high\-capacity and transformational donors.
* Models the role of a trusted philanthropic advisor and helps donors align their passions and ambitions with university priorities.
* Engages and prepares university leaders, volunteers, and advancement colleagues for successful donor interactions and solicitations.
* Ensures thoughtful stewardship and donor\-centered engagement opportunities that deepen donor relationships and inspire continued support.

**Operational Leadership**


* Provides oversight for the operational, financial, budgetary, and reporting functions of Main Campus Development.

**Reports to:** Board of Directors \| Status: Full\-time, Exempt

**Start Date:** January 1, 2027

**About Rolling Harvest Food Rescue**

Since 2010, Rolling Harvest Food Rescue has connected local farms' fresh, healthy surplus produce to food\- and nutrition\-insecure residents throughout Bucks County, PA and neighboring counties. Through farm\-based gleaning, produce rescue, growing, and distribution programs, Rolling Harvest partners with dozens of local growers and dozens of hunger\-relief sites — including food pantries, community kitchens, shelters, and low\-income senior housing — to deliver fresh produce free of charge. The nonprofit organization also facilitates nutrition education and awareness of food insecurity, food waste, and sustainable agriculture. Rolling Harvest envisions an equitable, local, and sustainable food system in which abundant access to fresh, healthy food is a fundamental right, not a privilege.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director (ED) is the chief executive officer of Rolling Harvest Food Rescue and works in partnership with the Board of Directors to advance the organization's mission. The ED provides strategic leadership, oversees daily operations, manages staff and volunteers, leads fundraising and development, and serves as the primary public face of the organization. This is an opportunity for a mission\-driven leader to guide a well\-established, respected grassroots nonprofit through its next stage of growth and impact.

* Serve as the primary spokesperson with media, government officials, and community partners. Oversee all social media messaging.
* Report regularly to the Board of Directors and support Board development and governance.
* Champion the organization's nutrition education and food\-waste awareness initiatives.

**Qualifications**

* 5\+ years of nonprofit management, hunger\-relief, agricultural, or related community\-impact experience involving strategic planning; direct executive leadership experience preferred
* Strong interpersonal skills, ability to manage others and build collaborations
* Ability to handle multiple responsibilities, prioritize work, solve problems, and operate under time and work volume pressure
* Demonstrated success in fundraising, grant writing, major gifts, and donor cultivation

* Experience building and maintaining partnerships and relationships with diverse stakeholders — farmers, hunger relief organizations, volunteers, funders, and legislators

* Commitment to building an inclusive organization and working with a diverse community
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
* Valid driver's license is required given regional travel

**Compensation \& Benefits** 

Compensation ranges from $80,000 to $90,000 commensurate with experience and education. Velox Clearing is a correspondent\-clearing broker\-dealer seeking an accomplished, hands\-on **Chief Operating Officer** to lead and scale its clearing operations. **Company Overview**  
Bloomington Developmental Learning Center is a vibrant, multi\-cultural child care facility on the south east side of Bloomington, Indiana dedicated to nurturing each child that comes through our door. Through a play\-based curriculum, we foster emotional, social, and cognitive growth for children from six weeks to five years old.

**Job Overview**

The Executive Director administers and manages the high\-quality child care program at BDLC, a not\-for\-profit organization, which has been in existence for more than 50 years. The Director provides vision and leadership for staff, under the supervision of the Board of Directors, to meet long\-term goals and maintain the fiscal integrity of the Center. This role reports to the President of the Board.

The Executive Director has the following responsibilities:

**1\. Organizational Leadership \& Culture**

* **Vision and leadership:** Provide clear leadership and direction for the organization by setting priorities, aligning people and resources, and fostering a culture that supports children, families, staff, and the long\-term success of BDLC.
* **Communication, Collaboration \& Support:** Support staff and families in navigating concerns, challenges, and transitions; Foster open communication, collaboration, and mutual respect across the organization; Address conflicts constructively and help teams navigate difficult situations in a productive and professional manner; Partner with the Office Administrator and Curriculum Coordinators to align priorities, solve problems, and support staff and families.
* **Board, Family \& Community Engagement**: Build and maintain positive, professional relationships with families, Board members, and community partners; Partner with the Board by providing timely organizational updates, participating in Board meetings, and supporting effective governance and decision\-making; Build and maintain positive relationships with community partners, professional organizations, and the broader Bloomington community to support BDLC's mission and long\-term success.

* **Policy \& Process Improvement**: In collaboration with the BDLC administrative team, implement program policies and procedures consistently, ensuring teachers and staff understand and follow established expectations; In collaboration with the BDLC board of directors, regularly evaluate program processes to identify opportunities for improvement

Posting Details
  
  

INTERVIEWS ARE ANTICIPATED TO BE CONDUCTED WITHIN TWO WEEKS OF CLOSING DATE
  
  

Please visit us at www.IndianArtsandCulture.org
  
  

Created in 1978 by the New Mexico Legislature, the Department of Cultural Affairs represents New Mexico's dedication to preserving and celebrating the cultural integrity and diversity of our state. The Department oversees a broad range of New Mexico's arts and cultural heritage agencies. These include 15 divisions representing a variety of programs and services.
  
Why does the job exist?
  
  

The Museum of Indian Arts and Culture (MIAC) is a center of stewardship, knowledge, and understanding of the artistic, cultural, and intellectual achievements of the diverse Indigenous peoples of the Greater Southwest. MIAC's mission is achieved by inspiring the public to learn more about the vibrant cultures of the Southwest, caring for and interpreting the collection, and collaboration with the Indigenous people of the Southwest. The Deputy Director assists the Executive Director in the administrative and strategic operation of the museum, including the Laboratory of Anthropology, Center for New Mexico Archaeology (CNMA), and Museum Hill Cafe.
  
How does it get done?
  
  

The Deputy Director oversees operations of the Museum, Library of Laboratory of Anthropology, and the Archaeological Repository at the CNMA. Responsibilities span a wide range of activities including, but not limited to, strategic planning, grant and annual budget preparation, preservation of and access to collections, security and visitor services, human resources and personnel policies, and management of facilities including planning maintenance and coordinating repairs. Projects are completed through close collaboration with other Department of Cultural Affairs bureaus and partners, including Facility Management Bureau, Museum Resources Division, and Museum of New Mexico Foundation. The Deputy Director represents the Museum to the public, Museum members, associated foundations, and the State of New Mexico in the Director's absence and as delegated by the Director with all the constituencies affiliated with the Museum.
  
Who are the customers?
  
  

Museum visitors include local, national, and international learners of all ages. MIAC seeks to be an inclusive and accessible museum that welcomes all of our public. Through continued collaboration, MIAC has maintained and strengthened relationships with members of the 23 tribes located in New Mexico's nineteen Pueblos, three Apache Tribes, and the Navajo Nation, as well as native nations in Colorado, Arizona and Texas. After nearly 100 years since the founding of the Laboratory of Anthropology, MIAC has a passionate community of supporters.

Bachelor's Degree in a relevant field of study from an accredited college or university and nine (9\) years of professional level experience operating within parameters and guidelines directly related to the purpose of the position defined by the agency at the time of recruitment. A hiring agency will designate a portion of the required experience to include supervisory and/or specialized experience. Any required licensure, certification or registration shall be defined at the time of recruitment and will be in addition to the above requirements.

The Executive Director of QCORE serves as the head of a university\-wide research institute and works closely with affiliated faculty and staff to build and lead a successful program advancing research and scientific discovery in quantum science, engineering, and business.  

  

QCORE’s primary objective is to empower Montana’s quantum ecosystem by uniting cutting\-edge research, industry partnerships, and community engagement – enabling breakthrough technologies that shape the future of quantum innovation. The vision of QCORE is to lead Montana’s transformation into a global powerhouse for quantum\-enabled technologies by 2035, fostering economic growth, academic excellence and a resilient, future\-focused workforce.  

  

QCORE exists to steward the development of transformative quantum technologies in service to the common good. Strategic partnerships serve as the mechanism for QCORE to strengthen relationships between industry, research and innovators – growing collaboration and creating shared opportunities for beneficial technology innovations.

At Kids Connection, We are passionate about our work and know that we are creating a positive impact in the community. If you are passionate about your work, want to make the community a better place, and develop your leadership skills this is the place for you!

**What qualification are we looking for?**

At Kids Connection we strive to ensure our employees are a good fit based on their strengths, interests, and future goals.

The successful candidate will have the following:

**Education/Certifications/Credentials/Professional Registration**

* Post\-secondary diploma in a related field
* Director Certification (Required)
* Standard Child Care First Aid with CPR
* Minimum 2 years of work experience in a management role
* Police Information Check
* 3 professional references

**Experience**

* Supervisory experience, including human resources functions such as recruitment, hiring, coaching and termination
* Leadership experience (within a child care environment preferred)

**Knowledge \& Skills**

* Ability to fluently use the entire MS Office suite
* Ability to act professionally in all situations, representing Kids Connection according to its core values
* Able to deal with difficult situations and complaints with confidence
* Excellent customer services skills
* Excellent organizational, time management, verbal and written communication skills
* Well\-developed interpersonal skills; ability to work effectively as a team to achieve optimal results
* Self\-motivated with the ability to direct personal performance to achieve desired results
* Ability to work without constant direct supervision
* Knowledge of State Child Care Act and Regulations
* Leadership skills

5\. **Outcome Thinking**: Visualizes, understands and articulates Kids Connections outcomes and formulates strategies, plans and actions for achievement

6\. **Quality Focus:** Ensures Kids Connections programs and services are superior

7\. **Teamwork**: Actively builds teams and encourages open relationships for maximum organizational effectiveness

This position is responsible for the day\-to\-day operation of Daycare/Before \& After School Care program. Responsibilities include:

* Adhere to license plan for site(s) responsible for

* Review licensing standards on a quarterly basis

* Resolve areas of non\-compliance immediately, under the guidance of the Senior Site Director and Childcare/or Before \& After School Care Program owners

Posting Information
**Posting Number** PG194902EP
  

**Internal Recruitment** No
  

**Working Title** Executive Director of Philanthropy
  

**Anticipated Hiring Range** Commensurate with education and experience.

**Job Location** Raleigh, NC
  

**Department** Dean's Office \- Poole College Of Management
  

**About the Department**
North Carolina State Universitywas founded in 1887 with the purpose of creating economic, societal and intellectual prosperity for the people of North Carolina. Today, NC State is the largest university in North Carolina, with more than 40,500 high\-performing students, more than 10,000 preeminent faculty and staff and more than 310,000 dedicated alumni. NC State is a **Research One (R1\)** university known for its leadership in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. We’re also at the forefront of teaching and discovery in agriculture, business, design, education, humanities and social sciences, natural resources, textiles and veterinary medicine. NC State is **consistently named** as one of the best values in higher education, and many of our programs are ranked at the top of their respective disciplines. We take a great deal of **pride** in our collaborative, supportive and collegial team culture. All staff are provided opportunities for training and professional development, with an eye to personalized career growth.  

This is an opportunity for a strategic, relationship\-driven advancement leader to partner with a dynamic dean, an engaged college community, and a committed University Advancement team to shape the next chapter of philanthropic growth for Poole College.  

The Poole College of Management actively engages with industry, alumni, and academic partners to create an innovative and collaborative environment that advances learning, scholarship, service, and real\-world impact. We’re deeply rooted in NC State’s history as a university that excels at science, technology, engineering, and math.  

Our college’s varied student body — over 4,800 students — hails from across North Carolina, the United States, and the world. Our faculty are thought leaders and field\-tested experts with enduring ties to the world of business.  

Poole College of Management has six academic departments: Accounting: Economics; Finance; Information, Technology, Operations, and Analytics; Marketing; and Management, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship. We offer bachelor’s degrees in accounting, business administration, economics; master’s degrees in accounting, business administration (MBA), economics, management (including specialized degrees); as well as a doctoral degree in economics. Among our non\-degree programs, we offer Executive Education and graduate certificates.  

The college houses six initiatives fostering research, learning, and corporate engagement: Business Analytics Initiative, Business Sustainability Collaborative, Enterprise Risk Management Initiative, Entrepreneurship Clinic, Financial Literacy Initiative, and Supply Chain Resource Cooperative. The college is fully accredited by the AACSB.  

To learn more about our College, visit: **https://poole.ncsu.edu**

As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our **Employee Value Proposition**and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone.

* **Tuition** and **Academic Assistance**
* **And so much more!**

Attain Work\-life balance with our **Childcare** benefits, **Wellness \& Recreation Membership**, and **Wellness Programs** that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community.  

  

*Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part\-Time or Full\-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered.*

The Poole College of Management at NC State University seeks an accomplished and collaborative advancement leader to serve as its Executive Director of Philanthropy. This senior leadership position provides strategic direction and oversight for the College’s comprehensive fundraising program while maintaining an active role in cultivating and securing significant philanthropic support.  

  

Reporting to the Dean of the Poole College of Management, with a dotted\-line reporting relationship to the Assistant Vice Chancellor for University Development, the Executive Director will lead a team of five philanthropy professionals and collaborate closely with University Advancement, faculty and College leadership, alumni, corporate and foundation partners, volunteers, and other key stakeholders.  

  

The Executive Director will develop and execute strategies to expand philanthropic support for the College’s priorities, strengthen the donor pipeline, and increase major, leadership\-level, and transformational giving.

jobs.description:
**Mentor Community Services**, a part of the Sevita family, provides community\-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission\-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived. **Program Director, IDD Services**  

Have you been looking for a fantastic role to continue your career path in Social and Human Services? Look no further. This role is critical to our success and exemplifies the wonderful mission driven work we do here every day.  

  

* Manage the day\-to\-day operations of one to four programs in a community including organization and implementation of direct supports, person\-centered planning, and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, recruiting, retention, staffing, training, safety, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.
* Manage program staff members including performance evaluations, scheduling, and orientation.
* Make recommendations and/or decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, corrective action, and terminations.
* Manage the implementation of program planning; monitor delivery of services and supports; ensure services are consistent, engaging, and relevant to the individuals served.
* Must be available on\-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.


***Qualifications:***  



* Bachelor's degree and two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.
* An equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Other education, experience, training, licensure, or certification per state requirements or as required by applicable regulations.
* Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
* Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to multi\-task to meet deadlines.
* Effective communication skills to manage relationships.
* A reliable, responsible attitude and a compassionate approach.


***Why Join Us?***  



* Full, Part\-time, and As Needed schedules available.
* Full compensation/benefits package for full\-time employees.
* 401(k) with company match.
* Paid time off and holiday pay.
* Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.
* Enjoy job security with nationwide career development and advancement opportunities.


***Pay:*** starts at $47,840\.00 annually.


**We have a rewarding work environment with awesome co\-workers – come join our team –** ***Apply Today!***

**Position Overview**

Executive Director provides leadership and management to ensure the organization fulfills its mission. This role requires broad oversight of operations, staff supervision, program continuity, financial accountability, and community engagement.

The Executive Director partners closely with the Board of Directors to sustain organizational health and prepare for the onboarding of permanent leadership. Executive Director will work closely with the faculty, staff, and contractors to strengthen infrastructure and position the Bowen Center for long\-term success.

The Bowen Center's work is grounded in Bowen Family Systems Theory, and this role requires a leader who can operate effectively within that framework and culture. The Executive Director’s performance will be evaluated by the Board of Directors annually.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Leadership \& Administration**

* Provide mission\-aligned leadership to the organization.
* Principal decision maker on key areas of management and programming.
* Lead, manage, support, and collaborate with staff, faculty and the Board of Directors ensuring clear communication and positive work environment.
* Build operational and technical continuity and institutional memory across staffing, systems, and annual workflows.
* Implement Board policies and maintain continuity of strategic plan activities.
* Oversee daily operations and maintain efficient, effective service delivery.

**Program Development \& Implementation** 

* Ensure the continuity and quality of educational programs grounded in Bowen theory.
* Maintain program schedules, communications, and promotional materials.
* Monitor program outcomes and provide updates to the Board.
* Partner effectively with the Bowen Center's volunteer faculty who lead conferences training programs, and educational offerings.
* Support the Center's mix of online, hybrid, and in\-person programming.
* Foster faculty development and support efforts to attract and cultivate emerging and local faculty

**Financial Management**

* Efficiently manage the operating budget in collaboration with the Treasurer/Finance Committee.
* Oversee reporting, compliance, forecasting, and financial accountability.
* Maintain donor and funder relationships; ensure timely reporting obligations.
* Develop and implement strategy for fundraising, including grant opportunities.

**Community Relations \& Outreach**

* Represent the organization with funders, partners, alumni, and community stakeholders.
* Maintain relationships with collaborating organizations and networks.
* Support the organization's in\-person presence in the District, Maryland, and Virginia area.

**Board Relations \& Governance**

* Serve as primary liaison between faculty and the Board.
* Provide regular updates on finances, operations, and program status, including staffing and organizational continuity.
* Support Board committees.
* Partner effectively with the Board on organizational priorities.

**Organizational Capacity Building**

* Document systems, policies, and processes for continuity.
* Identify organizational strengths, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
* Ensures the staffing model supports a sustainable team structure.
* Support succession planning and leadership continuity for the organization over time.

**Qualifications**

* At least a master’s degree in mental health, family therapy, organizational development, or related field
* Demonstrated understanding of and commitment to Bowen Family Systems Theory.
* Minimum of 5 years of experience in nonprofit management or leadership preferred.
* Previous experience in effective fiscal management, forecasting, fundraising, and grant management and grant writing.
* Effective interpersonal and communication abilities.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and relevant digital tools.
* Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively with boards, staff, faculty, and contractors

**Personal Qualities**

* Grounded in Bowen theory for a thinking approach to leadership and problem\-solving.
* Ability to manage organizational and personal anxiety during periods of change.
* Flexible, adaptive, and collaborative leadership style.
* Commitment to continuous learning and professional growth.
* Ability to build trust across board, faculty, and staff relationships.
* Ability to balance operational execution with longer\-term organizational development.

Additional Considerations Candidates may maintain private practice or consulting work alongside the role, provided, the responsibilities of the position and the 35\-hour weekly commitment are fully met.

new_jobs.title: Director of Operations
new_jobs.description:
Eastside Academy is creating a Director of Operations role for the first time as a deliberate investment in our organizational capacity and future. Until now, many of these responsibilities have been carried by the Executive Director alongside broader executive leadership responsibilities. This new role brings them together under a dedicated leader who can strengthen the systems, people, and infrastructure supporting the entire organization. The Director will join organizational leadership, lead an existing Operations Team, and build an operating environment in which people have the clarity, information, and support they need to do their best work.


### **About Eastside Academy**


Education is more than a basic right – it's essential to our ability to thrive. However, life's challenges can often stand in the way through no fault of our own. We believe that every student deserves access to holistic and wraparound care. Eastside Academy was created as a refuge and place of growth for high school students who may not fit the mold of traditional schools. We are different by design. Our unique and innovative approach to student life reaches beyond traditional education models. We provide an individualized education plan and holistic counseling to all students. Through our housing program, we can provide a safe and stable home environment for students with greater needs.
### **Description**


**Director of Operations**
==========================

**Location:** Bellevue, Washington

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Status:** Full\-time, exempt

**Salary:** $100,000–$115,000 annually

**Build the systems that allow a mission to flourish**
======================================================


Eastside Academy is creating a Director of Operations role for the first time as a deliberate investment in our organizational capacity and future.


Until now, many of these responsibilities have been carried by the Executive Director alongside broader executive leadership responsibilities. This new role brings them together under a dedicated leader who can strengthen the systems, people, and infrastructure supporting the entire organization.


The Director will join organizational leadership, lead an existing Operations Team, and build an operating environment in which people have the clarity, information, and support they need to do their best work.

**About Eastside Academy**
==========================


Eastside Academy is a nonprofit alternative high school and support program in Bellevue, Washington. Our mission is to inspire change in the lives of youth through high school education, counseling, recovery, housing, and life skills in a Christ\-centered environment.


Our students often come to Eastside Academy after not finding meaning, value, or success in traditional school settings. We walk alongside students and families through an integrated model of education, mental health care, and relational support that helps young people rediscover hope, purpose, and the possibility of a different future.

**What winning looks like**
===========================


The Director of Operations creates an organization in which the systems supporting the mission are dependable, visible, appropriately owned, and increasingly proactive. Staff spend less energy navigating operational friction, leaders have trustworthy information, risks are addressed early, and organizational growth does not require proportional increases in complexity.


Success means that:

  

* Facilities, technology, vendors, and administrative systems function reliably.
* Financial processes are accurate, timely, and well controlled.
* Employees experience clear and dependable people systems.
* Risks, compliance requirements, and recurring deadlines are addressed proactively.
* The Operations Team demonstrates increasing ownership and effectiveness.
* Routine operational matters no longer require the Executive Director’s involvement.
* EA’s systems become more scalable and less dependent on individual staff knowledge.

**What you will lead**
======================

### **Organizational Operations \+ Infrastructure**


Build and improve organization\-wide workflows, calendars, facilities, technology, purchasing, vendor relationships, and administrative systems. Clarify ownership, coordinate cross\-functional handoffs, remove operational friction, and lead Operations\-owned logistics for major organizational events and transitions.

### **Financial Operations \+ Stewardship**


Lead the Office Manager \+ Financial Administrator and oversee reliable financial\-administration systems. Partner with external accounting professionals, strengthen internal controls, monitor spending, support budgeting and forecasting, and provide leaders with trustworthy financial information for decision\-making.

### **People Operations \+ Organizational Support**

new_jobs.title: Senior Vice President & Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
**Who is the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra?**  

Known for its artistic excellence for more than 130 years, today the PSO is the region’s national and international cultural ambassador. A two\-time 2018 GRAMMY® Award\-winning orchestral ensemble credited with a rich history of concerts, performances, and recordings with the world’s finest conductors and musicians, the PSO consistently demonstrates a genuine commitment to Pittsburgh’s citizens, regional communities, and vibrant cultural scene. The internationally acclaimed Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra (PSO) engages audiences of all ages through unparalleled live musical experiences, community collaborations, and educational programming that enrich every life with great music.  

  

**JOB PURPOSE AND REPORTING STRUCTURE:**  

The Senior Vice President \& Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a key strategic and operational partner with the CEO and other organizational leadership in decision making and fulfilling the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra’s mission and goals. The COO is responsible for executing on annual and long\-term plans of the PSO through leadership and supervision in the following areas: artistic planning, strategic planning, orchestra\-, stage\-, and facility\-operations, electronic media, technology, orchestra personnel, labor relations, community programs, business intelligence, and general operations. The COO is part of the senior leadership team and works closely with the CEO, the CFO, the CDO, the CREO, the Music Director, the Board of Directors and other members of the leadership team on the execution of mission and strategic direction of the organization.  

  

**Direct Reports:** Vice President of Artistic Planning, Vice President of Operations, Vice President of Information Technology, Senior Vice President of Learning \& Engagement, Director of Commercial \& Popular Programming and Executive Administrative Associate.  

  

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES:**  

Leadership – the COO provides organizational leadership with a focus on daily internal operations as well as partnering with the C\-Suite on strategic planning for the future. The COO provides organizational leadership in the CEO’s absence and is the public face of the organization in the CEO’s absence. The COO provides general oversight of the PSI’s management operating system to ensure that planning processes, management controls, and internal communications effectively deliver the business of the PSI.  

  

Span of Control \- the COO supervises and directs all departments responsible for planning, developing and executing the Symphony seasons, Heinz Hall programming and operations, as well as activities related to education, electronic media and community programs. They work closely with the CFO and CEO on budget development and monitoring as well as long\-range financial planning for operational expenses. The COO also works in conjunction with senior leadership on the development and execution of the strategic plan, community projects, community relationships, run out and tour relationships as well as fundraising and marketing and communications when appropriate.  

  

Capital Projects \- The COO provides executive leadership and oversight for the PSO’s capital projects, ensuring investment strategies align with corporate objectives, operational priorities, growth initiatives, and long\-term financial goals. Direct capital planning and resource allocation processes across departments to maximize return and support sustainable organizational growth. Partner with executive leadership and key stakeholders to develop business cases, assess risks, establish funding priorities, and make strategic decisions regarding major capital investments.  

  

Staff Development and Management – The COO is responsible for ensuring that the departments are staffed appropriately and within the financial forecasts. The COO ensures that performance expectations are clearly defined, measured and if needed addressed. The COO, in conjunction with department leadership, identifies opportunities for employee growth and training. The COO leads the efforts to ensure that the work environment allows staff to perform, thrive and succeed.  

  

Labor Relations – The COO, in conjunction with the CEO, CFO, CREO and VP of Operations, is responsible for the labor relations management on behalf of the Symphony and for developing and maintaining collaborative working relationships with the labor unions working within the organization. This includes working closely with the VP of Operations and CREO on regular contract management, grievance processes and the collective bargaining negotiations process with seven unions. The COO ensures that the collective bargaining processes are aligned with the organizational direction strategies and goals. The COO also works with the CEO, VP of Operations and Director of Orchestra Personnel on individual contract negotiations with PSO musicians.  

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:*** College degree required, advanced degree and musical background preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of increasing responsibility in operational leadership and strategic planning.
* At least 8 years of experience in arts management, preferably in orchestra management.
* At least 5 years of experience in a senior management role with a professional arts organization.
* Demonstrated experience in motivating, managing and developing teams.
* Experience with large capital projects.
* Experience with labor negotiations and collective bargaining agreements.
* Working knowledge of orchestra repertoire and orchestra operations.

**Compensation and Location:**  

This is a full\-time exempt position with an annual salary between $200,000 \- $270,000 depending upon experience. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes paid holidays, paid time off, employer paid health benefits, as well as retirement savings options with an employer match. new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer / Integrator
new_jobs.description:
**Turbo Tim’s is growing, and we need a COO who can help turn big ideas into a great company at scale.**

**I’m Turbo Tim. In EOS and Rocket Fuel terms, I’m the textbook Visionary. I see possibilities everywhere, move fast, and love trying things the automotive industry hasn’t tried. I need a true Integrator beside me: someone who loves people, brings clarity to complexity, makes decisions, builds strong leaders, and turns ideas into results. You’ll be empowered to lead the business and tell me when an idea needs a better plan.**

**We’re an independent, multi\-location automotive company built around Cars, Cats, and Community. We’re expanding quickly, building a YouTube channel that shows what shop life can be, and developing a software company aimed at improving this industry. Depending on your strengths and interests, you could help shape those ventures too. We put on community events like Car Extravaganza and Crushawhirl, and our team volunteers because giving back is part of who we are. There’s a lot happening here, and the right person will help us grow it without losing what makes it special.**

**Our values are Care, CommUNITY, Trust, Innovation, and FUN. They have to show up in how we treat customers, develop employees, solve problems, and make decisions. We take employee feedback seriously: we track eNPS, listen to what drives it, and keep changing how we work to make this a better place for our people.**

**What you’ll own**
-------------------

* **Lead day\-to\-day operations across our locations and help build the systems, accountability, and leadership capacity needed for continued growth.**
* **Be the Integrator: turn vision into priorities, align the leadership team, follow through, and help us decide what deserves our attention now.**
* **Coach and grow our leaders. Build a company where people know what success looks like and have the support to reach it.**
* **Own operational performance and work with the team to improve the customer experience, financial results, and execution across the business.**
* **Use EOS tools and a healthy leadership cadence to surface issues, make decisions, and keep us moving.**
* **Protect and strengthen our culture as we add people, locations, and new ventures.**

**You might be our person if**
------------------------------

* **You’ve led people and operations through meaningful growth, and you can balance big\-picture thinking with consistent follow\-through.**
* **You understand EOS and the Visionary/Integrator relationship in Rocket Fuel, ideally because you’ve lived it.**
* **You’re direct, kind, calm under pressure, and genuinely good at getting the best out of people.**
* **You can challenge a passionate founder, earn trust across a team, and make ambitious ideas executable.**
* **You’re excited to bring a fresh perspective to automotive. Experience outside the automotive industry is especially welcome.**
* **You care about culture and employee feedback as much as you care about a scorecard.**

**Our previous COO has been an amazing Integrator and person. He set a high bar. At times we wondered how we could possibly offer him more room to grow, and he kept growing anyway. Those are big shoes to fill. You won’t be expected to fill them alone: we’ll support your development, give you room to lead, and expect you to invest just as deeply in the growth of our people.**

**If you want to lead a company that’s growing fast, trying new things, and doing real good in the community, we’d love to meet you. Apply with your résumé and a short note about why the Visionary/Integrator partnership appeals to you.**

new_jobs.title: Executive Director, Chief Operations Officer - Aetna Better Health of Maryland
new_jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

**Position Summary**


Aetna Better Health is Aetna’s Medicaid managed care plan. Backed by over 30 years of experience managing the care of those with a broad array of health care needs, our Medicaid plans have demonstrated that getting the right help when you need it is essential to better health. That’s why Aetna® Medicaid plans include the guidance and support needed to connect our members with the right coverage, resources, and care. We are focused on enhancing quality and population health outcomes while integrating CVS assets to bring accessible healthcare to our members.

  

Aetna Better Health of Maryland is seeking an experience leader with vast operational knowledge of Medicaid for its state\-wide managed Medicaid business in the role of Chief Operations Officer (COO). The COO role will be strategic and committed to developing colleagues as well as relentlessly pursuing change that is best for the organization and its customers. The COO role will collaborate with the CEO to develop the strategic vision of the Health Plan, policies \& procedures, and operational objectives including leading RFP readiness efforts. The COO will oversee high level strategic and operational activities of various plan functional areas which include traditional service operations (Claims, Provider Services, Information Technology, Grievance \& Appeals and Member Services) as well as Medical Management (Quality, Network, Compliance, Health Equity, Medical Directors, Utilization Management, Vendor Management). These activities may include colleague productivity, building and maintaining a highly inclusive and diverse culture as well as ensuring team members thrive and organizational outcomes are met.

 **Major Responsibilities**

* Partner with the Plan CEO to drive successful growth, operational excellence, and overall business performance.
* Oversee financial management of the health plan, including budget accountability, revenue target achievement, and P\&L performance.
* Collaborate with corporate functional leaders and centralized shared services teams to drive operational effectiveness and business results.
* Provide leadership and oversight across core operational areas, including: Claims systems and processing, Third\-Party Liability (TPL) and Coordination of Benefits (COB), Pharmacy claims operations and their impact on total cost of care, Call center operations and performance and Encounter data management and processing.
* Lead and support provider operations activities, including: Provider data management, Credentialing, Provider relations, Network development and contracting, and Value\-based care contracting and performance initiatives.
* Drive strategies that enhance provider experience while managing medical costs and improving operational outcomes.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable state contracts, regulations, executive orders, and healthcare industry requirements.
* Partner with Government Affairs and Legal teams to address regulatory, legislative, and compliance\-related matters.
* Serve as a key advocate with internal stakeholders, state regulators, policymakers, and other external partners.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with community\-based advocacy organizations and industry stakeholders.
* Oversee communications and engagement strategies for members and providers.
* Support and promote community\-based programs that address Social Determinants of Health (SDOH), including housing, employment, Community Health Workers (CHWs), Peer support specialists and nutrition and food access initiatives.
* Apply expertise in the integration of physical and behavioral healthcare, with a strong understanding of the unique needs of the Medicaid population.
* Represent the organization externally with regulatory agencies, state departments, community partners, and other key stakeholders.
* Act as a trusted executive leader and extension of the CEO, providing strategic leadership both internally and externally.

  

The COO will oversee business operations performance and employee productivity, building and maintaining our highly inclusive and diverse culture, ensuring team members thrive, and organizational outcomes are met. Lead people, build/maintain relationships while driving talent and culture development.

 **Required Qualifications**


The candidate will have a strong work ethic, be a self\-starter, and be able to be highly productive in a dynamic, collaborative environment. This position offers broad exposure to all aspects of the company’s business, as well as significant interaction with all the business leaders. The candidate will be expected to have the following key attributes:

  

* 10\+ years of work experience reflecting a proven track record of government programs such as Medicaid, Medicare, or Dual Eligible plans.
* 5\+ years of experience in executive leadership roles with proven track record of proficiency in the operational competencies noted.
* Demonstrated success with C\-suite stakeholders.
* Ability to work collaboratively across many teams, prioritize demands from those teams, synthesize information received, and generate meaningful conclusions.
* Ability to conceive innovative ideas or solutions to meet clients’ requirements.
* Excellent communication and relationship management skills and being able to express thoughts in an organized and articulate manner.
* Ability to build a climate of trust and respect with regulators, external stakeholders, as well as colleagues, peers, and our internal growth partners.

Global Government Relations (GGR) is housed within Corporate Responsibility and is responsible for developing and implementing a comprehensive policy, regulatory and advocacy strategy on behalf of JPMorgan Chase. This includes engaging in balanced advocacy with regulators and policymakers, understanding and providing thought leadership on how policies affect the firm's clients and economic growth overall, and governing internal coordination among regions and lines of business on global regulatory reform issues.


As an Executive Director within the Federal Government Relations (FGR) team, you will be working in collaboration with the Global Government Relations Team to oversee legislative activities, scrutinize policy and political trends, and enlighten Congressional and Executive Branch public officials on matters of mutual interest. Your responsibilities will also include closely liaising with the firm's business lines and clients to comprehend emerging issues, and to devise, support, and advocate for the progression of public policy priorities that influence the firm and our clients.

new_jobs.title: Program Director
new_jobs.description:
**Mentor Community Services**, a part of the Sevita family, provides community\-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission\-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived. **Program Director, IDD Services**  

Have you been looking for a fantastic role to continue your career path in Social and Human Services? Look no further. This role is critical to our success and exemplifies the wonderful mission driven work we do here every day.  

  

* Manage the day\-to\-day operations of one to four programs in a community including organization and implementation of direct supports, person\-centered planning, and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, recruiting, retention, staffing, training, safety, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.
* Manage program staff members including performance evaluations, scheduling, and orientation.
* Make recommendations and/or decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, corrective action, and terminations.
* Manage the implementation of program planning; monitor delivery of services and supports; ensure services are consistent, engaging, and relevant to the individuals served.
* Must be available on\-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.


***Qualifications:***  



* Bachelor's degree and two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.
* An equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Other education, experience, training, licensure, or certification per state requirements or as required by applicable regulations.
* Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
* Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to multi\-task to meet deadlines.
* Effective communication skills to manage relationships.
* A reliable, responsible attitude and a compassionate approach.


***Why Join Us?***  



* Full, Part\-time, and As Needed schedules available.
* Full compensation/benefits package for full\-time employees.
* 401(k) with company match.
* Paid time off and holiday pay.
* Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.
* Enjoy job security with nationwide career development and advancement opportunities.


***Pay:*** starts at $47,840\.00 annually.


**We have a rewarding work environment with awesome co\-workers – come join our team –** ***Apply Today!***

  

Sevita is a leading provider of home and community\-based specialized health care. We believe that everyone deserves to live a full, more independent life. We provide people with quality services and individualized supports that lead to growth and independence, regardless of the physical, intellectual, or behavioral challenges they face.
  

  

We’ve made this our mission for more than 50 years. And today, our 40,000 team members continue to innovate and enhance care for the 50,000 individuals we serve all over the U.S.  

*As an equal opportunity employer, we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by law.*
